• outcome the individual requirements and overall inspection using the following criteria:
- outcome as “YES” when applicant meets all statutory requirements,

PROCESSES
Regulatory compliance inspections fall into two categories, both of which will be discussed below under the
following headings:
• Administrative inspections, and
• Public safety inspections.

heading: 6.1 Authority for inspections
text:
a. Under the Liquor Control and Licensing Act (LCLA):
For the purposes of conducting an inspection to determine compliance with the LCLA and its regulation, the
general manager may enter and inspect:
• establishment of any person set apart or used as a warehouse for the storage of liquor. This includes the
business location of a caterer where liquor is stored, and
• establishments licensed under the LCLA, including any area within the establishment where:
- liquor is manufactured, stored, or served
- events where a special event permit has been issued, and
- catered events in relation to which the caterer has been issued a catering authorization by the general
manager. A caterer may sell or serve liquor at a residence that is not a licensed establishment. Inspectors
are not authorized to inspect residential catering or special events.

[Liquor Control and Licensing Act, s.42]

b. Under the Cannabis Control and Licensing Act (CCLA):
For the purposes of conducting an inspection to determine compliance with the CCLA and its regulations, the
general manager may enter a Cannabis Retail Store and a Producer Retail Store, any place used by the licensee to
conduct their business (e.g.

heading: 6.1 Authority for inspections

: head office) and a conveyance owned or leased by the licensee and used in the
cannabis business, to do any of the following:
• inspect records required under this Act or by the terms and conditions of a licence to be kept by the licensee
or other records found in the licensee's establishment,
• remove the records referred to in paragraph (a) for the purposes of inspection or making copies or extracts,
• require a licensee to provide information relating to the inspection,
• require any person in the licensee's establishment, including patrons, to produce identification for the

• inspect the licensee's establishment and the operations carried on there,

heading: 6.2 Administrative inspections
text:
Administrative inspections are conducted primarily during daytime hours where the inspector is tasked to focus
primarily on the following administrative regulatory requirements:
a. Administrative Inspections for Liquor Licensees:
• Social Responsibility Materials - inspector ensures at least one social responsibility material is posted,
• Discussed Minors as Agents Program (MAP) - inspector ensures licensee is aware of MAP program,
• Drink Size/Minimum Pricing - inspector ensures drink size and pricing is compliant,
• Liquor Licence - inspector ensures the licence is valid and information on licence is correct and licence is
posted,
• Liquor Register - inspector confirms liquor register is kept, and that product is purchased from LDB,
• Floor Plan Accurately Depicts Physical Layout - inspector ensures blue line floor plan is available and
correctly depicts the current physical layout of the service area,
• Serving it Right - inspector ensures all staff selling/serving liquor or supervising the sale or service of
liquor hold valid Serving it Right certification,

b. Administrative Inspections for Cannabis Licensees:
• Product & Accessories Exterior Displays - Window displays of cannabis and cannabis accessories directed
to people outside the store is prohibited.

heading: 6.2 Administrative inspections
text:
Before entering the store, the Inspector will observe for
compliance.
• Advertising - inspector ensures advertising is compliant,
• Social Responsibility Materials - inspector checks to ensure any mandatory educational materials are
posted.
• Licence - inspector ensures the licence is valid and information on licence is correct and licence is posted,
• Floor Plan - inspector ensures blue line floor plan is available and correctly depicts the current physical
layout of the store,
• Security Requirements - inspector confirms physical security provisions continue to be met,
• Staff SIR Reviewed - inspector ensures licensee and staff who sell or supervise the sale of cannabis hold
valid Selling it Right certification,
• Cannabis Register - inspector confirms cannabis purchase records are kept and that all products for sale are
purchased under the licence number from LDB,
• Packaging - inspector ensures all product sold is in original packaging, and
• Smell Jars - inspector ensures compliance with use of smell jars where utilized,

heading: 6.3 Administrative inspection types
text:
1. Final Licence: conducted as a final step in the “new” licensing process. The procedure for the conduct of a
final inspection is detailed at “Conduct of Final Licence Inspections.”
2. Routine: used for all planned inspections of any licensed establishment that has not been inspected in
accordance with the C&E Division’s annual strategic plan and where the inspector’s intent is to check to
confirm the licensee’s administrative regulatory requirements have been met. The procedure for conducting
routine inspections of each licence type is detailed at “Conduct of Routine Inspections.”
3. Follow-up: used where the inspector physically attends and personally confirms voluntary compliance
because of a previous recent finding of non-compliance where a contravention was identified, and an
Electronic Notification of Non-Compliance was issued, and enforcement action was not recommended.
A follow-up inspection must occur within 90 days of the initial inspection where the contravention was
identified.
4. Remote community: used as an alternate to a physical on-site routine inspection of the licensed
establishment due to the establishment’s remote location and in consideration of the time and resource
impact on attending the remote location that may be prohibitive. The procedure for the conduct of a remote
community inspection is detailed at “Conduct of Remote Community Inspections.”

heading: 6.4 Administrative activities
text:
Ancillary to the ongoing delivery of the branch’s compliance and enforcement program, inspectors perform
several important administrative activities in support of service delivery. Those activities are recorded by the

inspector into the branch database under the heading “New Administrative Activities” for program quality
assurance and statistical reporting as described below:

1. BARWATCH/CAPE/OEC: where the inspector attended a local community “Barwatch” committee,
CAPE (committee to approve public event), or OEC (outdoor event committees) meeting, etc.
2. COURSE/TRAINING: where the inspector attended work related courses or training and pre-approved by
employer ONLY, (NOT to be used for completing employer mandated annual Learning Centre courses or
participation in branch working groups or projects, etc.),
3. ENFORCEMENT PROCESSES: where the inspector attended a branch enforcement hearing, or attended
an establishment to post signs, issue an Electronic Notification of Non-Compliance, hand deliver a NOEA
or obtain a signature on a Waiver. (Inspectors are NOT to record these administrative types of enforcement
processes as inspections),
4. POLICE LIAISON: used ONLY where the inspector meets with police specific to a liquor or cannabis
licence file, (NOT to be used for general introductions),
5. POLICE ROLL CALL: where an inspector presented information/education to police in a roll call format,
(NOT to be used to capture time in support of complaint investigations or general police liaison or
introductions),
6.

heading: 6.5 Recording a new administrative activity
text:
The inspector will record the activity in the inspector’s notebook and subsequently enter that information into
the branch database within 5 days from the date of the completion of the activity.

For each activity completed, the inspector will access the “New Administrative Activity” tab located in the
branch database under the C&E menu and complete the entry in accordance with the criteria listed beside each
activity type listed at “Administrative Activities.”

Note: The data entry of New Administrative Activities is NOT to be used to capture inspection planning, phone
calls, email review, travel time, vehicle repairs or re-fuelling, inspection or investigation data entry, report
writing, compliance meetings, etc.

heading: 6.6 Public safety inspections
text:
Liquor: public safety inspections of licensed establishments are generally scheduled and executed during the
later evening/early morning or during times when a licensed liquor establishment would be subject to a higher
number of patrons as a result of a special event such as sporting events, happy hour, or other occasions of
celebration, where the inspector is tasked to focus primarily on serious public safety violations including but not
limited to:
• intoxication,
• over-crowding,
• minors,
• unlawful liquor,
• unlawful activities or conduct,
• operating outside of licence purpose,
• operating outside licensed hours, and
• causing or contributing to disturbance of persons in the vicinity.

Cannabis: public safety inspections of a cannabis retail store and producer retail store are generally scheduled
and executed during the later evening and where the inspector is tasked to focus primarily on serious public
safety violations including but not limited to:
• intoxicated patrons,
• minors,
• unlawful cannabis,
• cannabis consumption,
• disorderly or unlawful conduct, and
• causing or contributing to disturbance of persons in the vicinity.

heading: 6.7 Public safety inspection types
text:
1. Public Safety: primarily used for inspections of establishments scheduled and executed in the later
evening/early morning, at peak operating times for the establishment, or at any time where establishments
may be promoting attendance to celebrate certain holidays or festive occasions such as Octoberfest or St.
Patrick’s Day; to view televised sporting events such as Ultimate Fighting or professional sports
championship series, tournaments or games. The procedure for the conduct of a public safety inspection is
detailed at “Conduct of Public Safety Inspections.”
2. Multi-agency: used where inspector either leads or participates in a multi-agency inspection consisting of
LCRB inspectors and at least one more regulatory agency or local police. In addition to enhancing and
contributing to communication and partnering initiatives as specified in “Program Overview,” multi-agency
inspections are an effective tool in the conduct of overt public safety inspections in cooperation with local
police and other regulatory agencies.
3. Special Permit Event (SEP): conducted to ensure the safety of the public who attend a special event by
ensuring compliance of the terms and conditions and within the parameters of the approved event security
plan. The procedure for the conduct of a special event inspection is detailed at “Conduct of a Special Event
Inspection.”
4. Covert: conducted as a result of intelligence that indicates the public may be at risk due to the operation of
the establishment or conduct or activities that may be occurring at an establishment.

heading: 6.7 Public safety inspection types
text:
The procedure for the
conduct of a covert inspection is detailed at “Conduct of a Covert Inspection.”
5. Minors as Agents Program (MAP): conducted to monitor compliance with the legislative prohibitions
against selling liquor or cannabis to minors. The procedure for the conduct of a MAP inspection is detailed at
“Conduct of a Minors as Agents Program (MAP) Inspection.”
6. Outside Licensed Hours: conducted where the branch has reason to believe a licensee may be selling or
serving liquor or cannabis outside of the authorized hours of service as established on their licence. The
procedure for the conduct of an outside hours of service inspection is detailed “Conduct of an Outside
Licensed Hours Inspection.”

heading: 6.8 Scheduling inspections
text:
In order to determine which establishments are higher priorities for inspection, the inspector on a regular basis
will review:
• any suspension penalties scheduled for establishments,
• police LPC’s/information received,
• public or industry complaints received,
• requests for final licence inspections,
• the list of establishments that have not been inspected within any period of time as established within the
C&E Division’s Annual Strategic Plan (e.g.: the preceding 24 months), or as may be modified at any time by
operational priority, and
• open-source information found on webpages, social media and print media.

heading: 6.9 Scheduling inspection times
text:
Inspections will be conducted at various times and on different days both during, and beyond, the operating
hours of an establishment. Inspectors will schedule inspection times based on the following factors:
• the proximity of establishments within a geographical area,

• estimated length of time for the inspection,
• operating hours of the establishment, and
• time of day in which previous contraventions or concerns occurred.

Inspectors will schedule inspections so as to minimize travel time between destinations. Where an establishment
has more than one licensed area, such as a hotel with both an FP restaurant and an LRS, the inspector will
generally inspect all licensed areas on one visit.

heading: 6.10 Prioritizing establishments for inspections
text:
Inspections are scheduled and planned so that branch resources are primarily focused on higher priority
establishments as well as with a goal of achieving division strategic objectives and operational measures and
time spent in planning and execution of inspections is used to best advantage. Higher priority establishments are
those with recent instances of non-compliance.

Inspectors will give a higher inspection priority to establishments where:
• the licensee is serving a suspension,
• complaints about the establishment have been received,
• a follow-up inspection is required as a result of a recent Electronic Notification of Non-Compliance where
non-compliance has been identified, or
• a new “Approval in Principle” licence applicant requires a final licence inspection be scheduled.

heading: 6.11 Planning for an inspection
text:
11. Prior to conducting an inspection, the inspector will review the branch database to become familiar with the
establishment and note areas that may require observation during the inspection. While planning an inspection,
the inspector will also make note of business hours and days of operation listed as public information.

The inspector will plan for the inspection by considering the following questions:

• are there any “Establishment Incident Alerts” in the branch database to be considered?
• what type of inspection is required?
• is the inspection the result of an LPC or a complaint? If so, what is the nature or content of the LPC or
complaint?
• should other persons be involved in the inspection? (e.g.: other inspectors or police)
• will it be necessary to speak with the licensee or authorized representative during the inspection?
• are there past concerns for which the licensee should have taken follow-up action? and
• what forms and materials will be required?

heading: 6.12 Conducting inspections
text:
As part of its role to supervise the operation of establishments, the branch conducts inspections. Inspections
provide an opportunity for inspectors to view how a licensee is operating the establishment and identify whether
the manner of operation is non-compliant or likely to lead to non-compliance. If potential compliance problems
are identified, the inspector can provide advice to the licensee on what steps to take to avoid future problems.
Inspections also assist in ensuring compliance with the legislation, regulation and terms and conditions of a
licence by providing evidence of ongoing branch interest and attention.

After each inspection where an Electronic Notification of Non-Compliance is issued, or a potential compliance
problem identified, the inspector will schedule a follow-up inspection to determine whether the licensee has
taken action to resolve the problem or prevent further occurrences of the contravention.

heading: 6.13 Recording inspections
text:
In general, inspectors will strive to record inspections directly on the branch mobile database immediately after
an inspection. Where the use of the mobile database is not feasible, such as lack of connectivity, the inspector

will record the information in the inspector’s notebook and subsequently enter that information into the branch
database. Administrative inspections must be entered the same day that the inspection occurs; Public
Safety/Covert Inspections must be entered on the same or next business day. Routine and MAP inspections
where no alleged contravention has been identified must be completed on the same day the inspection is
conducted.

For each inspection, the inspector will record:
• name of licensee/representative/manager or staff person with whom the inspector spoke,
• time in and time out,
• any conversations with the licensee/representative/manager or staff person specific to any non-compliance,
areas of potential concern or follow-up required, and
• certify regulatory inspection criteria has been met through completion of inspection regulatory checklist
within the inspection data entry screen.

heading: 6.14 Recording an attempted inspection
text:
An “Attempted Inspection” is selected as an outcome of an inspection job where the inspection did not take
place and used only where the inspector has physically attended an establishment’s licensed location to execute
an inspection. An attempted inspection is only selected where an inspection did not occur for a reason outside of
the control of the inspector. (i.e.: in the case of an administrative inspection, the establishment was closed upon
arrival of the inspector even though the establishment would normally be open as specified within their posted
hours of operation; or in the case of a public safety inspection, the inspector upon arrival and following protocol,
conducted a site risk assessment and determined that there was a potential for risk of harm to the inspector and
as such, the inspector decided to abort the inspection.) With sound inspection prioritizing, planning and
execution by the inspector “Attempted” inspection outcomes should be of a minimal occurrence.
Inspectors shall conduct routine administrative inspections for each licence type in accordance with the
procedures as specified in the below sub-sections:

heading: 6.21 Routine inspection of a liquor manufacturing site
text:
General:
A basic manufacturing license permits a licensee to sell product to other licensees as permitted through the
manufacturing agreement with the Liquor Distribution Branch. It allows a licensee to market and promote their
products offsite to licensees and the public and to set aside one or more interior areas where they may sell or
serve samples of their products to their patrons between 9 a.m. and 11 p.m.

The basic manufacturing license permits licensees to take patrons on guided tours of their establishment
between 9 a.m. and 11 p.m. The tour route is considered a service area which permits the service or sale of
samples to persons on the tour. The tours are permitted in any area of the business but are only permitted outside
if there are exterior features related to manufacturing, (e.g.: a vineyard).

Routine inspections of liquor manufacturing sites include the inspection of the production facility and any
endorsements the licensee may have (lounge, special event area, picnic area or on-site store).

heading: 6.24 Routine inspection of a market authorization event
text:
General:
Markets are an opportunity for licensees with the onsite store endorsement to provide samples and sell their
product at these events. An eligible market must consist of more than half of vendors who sell artisanal goods of
their own making, processed/prepared food, ready-to-eat food, or agricultural goods they produce, grow, or raise
themselves.

Requirements:
• On-site Store Endorsement: licensee must have an onsite store endorsement and apply through the One-
Stop for a market authorization; this authorization must be posted at the vendor booth during liquor service
hours,
• Market Eligibility: must ensure market is eligible (at least 6 vendors that do not sell/serve liquor); all
vendors must be artisans (making own items/agricultural goods they grow themselves),
• Liquor Service Hours: can only sell between 9 am and 11 pm,
• Liquor Products: may only sell products registered to the license,
• Liquor Sales: must be reported through the online store and staff must have their SIR,
• Liquor Service Area: defined sales area.

heading: 6.24 Routine inspection of a market authorization event
text:
The market authorization must be posted in a prominent place;
patrons cannot leave with unfinished samples and liquor must stay within the defined space.

Procedure:

• conduct a cursory inspection of the market to ensure there are at least six vendors not selling or serving
liquor

• identify themselves to the licensee or representative and inform them of the intent of the inspection.
• review the market authorization that must be posted in a prominent place within the designated area,
• review liquor service hours noted on the market authorization,
• review all products for sale or being offered as samples to ensure products are registered to the licence,
• review the sample sizes to ensure compliance,
• confirm with licensee and/or staff that the sale of liquor product is facilitated via the online store,
• verify staff selling/serving liquor have their SIR,
• inspect sales/sampling area (must be a defined area,

• observe liquor sales/consumption specifically relating to the control of patrons’ movement with samples,
• note time inspector departs vendor’s area.

heading: 6.27 Routine inspection of a manufacturer/agent take home sampling event
text:
General
The LCRB has established policy and licence terms and conditions respecting take home sampling events.

Policy
A manufacturer or agent licensee may conduct take home sampling events wherein the licensee may hand out
sealed product samples in public for home consumption. Take home sampling events are not permitted within a
licensed establishment or retail store.

No special provincial licence or permit is required by the licensee to run a take home sampling event however,
the licensee must obtain approval from the LCRB prior to the conduct of the event by submitting their event
plan.

Provincial law does not prohibit adults carrying unopened liquor in a public place and there is no requirement
that the unopened liquor be taken directly home by the person receiving it. Licensees should contact the
municipality, regional district, or First Nation with jurisdiction over the area where the event is going to be
conducted. Local governments may have their own bylaws, community standard practices and may wish to
allow, modify, restrict, or limit such events.

Take home sampling events are not public tastings, which is where the public consumes liquor at an event which
requires different application and approval requirements.

Procedure:
Where the branch approves a licensee to hold a take home sampling event, licensing staff will email the
applicable regional manager and regional supervisor responsible for the area the event will be located. The
regional manager/regional supervisor will notify the appliable inspector of the scheduled take home sampling
event.

heading: 6.27 Routine inspection of a manufacturer/agent take home sampling event
text:
The inspector will review the event plan to ensure the event is not being conducted at a licensed
establishment.

Where an inspection of a take home sampling event is conducted, the inspector will ensure:

• Approval: the licence of the event organizer is valid and information on licence is correct, and the event is
approved by the branch,
• Serving it Right: all staff providing liquor samples to the public hold valid Serving it Right certification,
• Intoxication: samples are not provided to intoxicated persons or persons showing signs of intoxication,
• Product samples: must be registered with LDB
• Sample sizes:
▪ sample sizes do not exceed maximum liquid volume restrictions,
▪ samples are not cooled,
▪ one sample per adult though use of a hand stamp,
▪ no open samples on site,
▪ public is advised the sample is for home consumption only,
▪ samples are affixed with a sticker or other devise indicating product to be consumed at home

➢ all contraventions will be addressed through written notification to the licensee,
➢ it is not essential to recommend enforcement action if other methods or compliance meeting can
achieve voluntary compliance,
• Resources/Financial Estimates,
➢ it is essential to identify human resources as early as possible for the following considerations:
- budget considerations,
- travel arrangements,
- assigning teams and areas of responsibilities,
• Inspection Procedures, Protocols and Safety
➢ audit projects are not to be intrusive. Licensees are trying to operate very demanding businesses.

heading: 6.30 Conduct of a manufacturing audit project inspection
text:
It
is important to gather the required information for the audit project while balancing the needs of the
licensee,
➢ if the licensee is in a critical stage of manufacturing, it may be prudent to return at a later hour. It is
critical to ascertain whether the delay would jeopardize the integrity of the inspection,
➢ safety of the inspection team is paramount. A review of the C&E Safety Procedures Manual prior to
commencing the audit project is an important inspection planning consideration and is highly
recommended, and
➢ all identified safety issues are to be documented and forwarded to the direct manager as soon as
possible.

heading: 6.31 Conduct of remote community inspections
text:
Remote Community “Routine” Inspections
While routine inspections of all licensed establishments at regular scheduled intervals is a desirable goal of the
Compliance and Enforcement Inspection Program, there are challenges in meeting this goal in the more remote
communities of the province where factors affect the inspector’s ability to physically attend an establishment.

Remote community inspections apply to establishments located in an area that is not readily accessible to the
inspector due to:
- excessive travel time,
- geography where the method of travel requires use of ferries, small charter boats or planes or assist from
RCMP,
- inclement weather,
- adverse travel conditions such as logging roads,
- budget constraints, and
- prior commitments or other assigned work priorities,

As such, licensed establishments in remote communities are subject to either less frequent inspections over
longer periods of time or require extensive resource allocation to attend remote communities which may not be
the best use of those resources. Generally, where a community is more than five (5) hours travel time from the
regional or satellite office and there are less than five (5) licensed establishments in the targeted community, the
inspector may conduct a remote community routine inspection:

Remote Community Inspections are to be carried out in accordance with division strategic plan and regional
priorities.

heading: 6.31 Conduct of remote community inspections
text:
Where the inspector has information to believe that an “on site” physical inspection is required (e.g.:

police concerns, complaints etc.), he/she will discuss this with the Regional Manager/Regional Supervisor and
put together a proposal for travel to the community.

On-site physical inspections of all establishments located in remote communities should be conducted at least
once every three (3) years and must be conducted once every five (5) years.

heading: 6.32 Remote community routine inspection general procedures
text:
General:
The following procedures apply to all remote community routine inspections of all licence types.

Procedure:
• Contact the local RCMP/police detachment responsible for the remote community and discuss any areas of
concern that the police may have with respect to compliance in their local licensed establishments,
• Contact the licensee for the establishment by phone and review all regulatory administrative requirements
with them using the checklists for each licence type,
• Confirm the licensee’s email address and email the licensee using the “Remote Community Inspection
Requirements Letter,” the list of documents, records and photos that the licensee would be required to
produce, or the inspector would be required to confirm for that licence type during an on-site routine
inspection, and request the licensee return to the inspector for verification of compliance.
a. Remote Community Inspection Requirements Letter will be sent by Dynamics. The Inspector
must check the "Send Remote Community Letter" box in Dynamics. This box will appear in the
"Activities" tab for the inspection.
• Upon receipt of the requested information upload photos/documents into the branch database in accordance
with branch records management policy, and
• Document in the branch database as a “remote community” inspection with detailed notes about how the
inspection was carried out (i.e.: over the phone, police contact including name of officer, discussion with
licensee including name of individual, etc.)

heading: 6.33 Remote community final licence inspection general procedures
text:
Remote Community “Final Licence” Inspections
In order to accommodate the needs of various licence applicants, it is sometimes necessary to conduct remote
final licence inspections. Although this is not the optimum solution to a final licence inspection, it is acceptable
to conduct a remote community final licence inspection in accordance with established procedures.

General:
Final licence inspection procedures of the various licence types are prescribed at “Final Licence Inspections.”
The following procedures apply to all remote community final licence inspections of all licence types.

Procedure:
The inspector will contact the applicant and:
• Review the AIP letter with the applicant,
• Provide the applicant with the Branch webpage link to the Terms and Conditions Handbook for the
licence type,
• Discuss the Minors as Agents Program and the restrictions on the employment of minors,
• Confirm the applicant’s email address and email the applicant using the “Remote Community Inspection
Requirements Letter”, the list of documents, records and photos that the applicant would be required to
produce, or the inspector would be required to confirm for that licence type during an on-site final licence
inspection, and request the applicant return to the inspector for verification of compliance.

heading: 6.33 Remote community final licence inspection general procedures
text:
(see section 5
this manual)
• Upon receipt of the requested information upload photos/documents into the branch database in
accordance with branch records management policy, and

• Document in the branch database as a “final licence” inspection with detailed notes about how the
inspection was carried out (i.e.: over the phone, discussion with licensee including name of individual,
etc.)
• The inspector will conduct a follow up inspection at the establishment within 6 months of the Remote
Community Final Licence Inspection to confirm that there are no discrepancies.

heading: 6.34 Dormant licence inspection
text:
Both section 92 of the Liquor Control and Licensing Regulation and section 27 of the Cannabis Licensing
Regulation establish a two-year period of limitation for which a licence may remain dormant before
cancellation, with some exceptions. The Branch must be aware of licensed establishments that are not in
operation to ensure compliance with the regulations.

Liquor inspectors may conduct inquiries or inspections to verify the establishment is closed and determine if it is
in compliance with the Act, regulations, and terms and conditions of the licence. Failure to abide by the T&Cs
of the licence may result in the cancellation of a liquor licence before the end of the dormancy period.

[Liquor Control and Licensing Act, s.49(5)]
[Liquor Control and Licensing Regulation, s.92]
[Cannabis Control and Licensing Act, s.37(5)]
[Cannabis Licensing Regulation, s.27]
[Terms and Conditions Handbooks]

Procedure:
To determine if a licence should be in dormancy, inspectors are to:
1. Access the licence in the branch database and review any inspections within the last 2 years and confirm
the establishment has been in operation. Where an application is in progress, (structural, change in
ownership, etc.) the inspector should contact licensing staff working on the application who may have
additional information to assist the inspector.
2. Where the establishment is within a convenient/short driving distance the inspector may attend the
establishment to confirm.
3.

heading: 6.34 Dormant licence inspection
text:
Where from the branch database the inspector cannot readily confirm the licence is in operation, the
inspector is to conduct a search of the establishment on social media (Google, Facebook etc.).
4. Where the inspector cannot determine on social media if the establishment is in operation the inspector will
contact the licensee.
5. In order to get the most accurate contact information for a licensee the inspector will need to:
• check the “Licence File” and obtain the contact information for the licensee (note: this contact
information is usually found in the first part of the application, normally referred to as “Licensee
Information”), and
• call the licensee to determine if the licence is operating the inspector may consider relevant information
such as sales records, stock levels, employee payroll, advertising, liquor purchases etc.
6. In the case of a liquor licence, the licensee confirms the establishment is still operational but purchasing
liquor under a different licence, the inspector is to note under the “Notes” tab in the main licence screen, the
licence number that the LDB purchases are routed through.
7. If the inspector has completed all the above steps and cannot confirm the operational status of the licence,
the inspector is to conduct a physical on-site inspection of the establishment.
8. Any issues or concerns that cannot be readily addressed by the inspector are to be referred to the RI or RM
for discussion or direction.
9.

heading: 6.34 Dormant licence inspection
text:
Inspectors may issue where the inspector has determined the licensee is not in compliance with the terms
and conditions respecting dormant licences. (see “Fail to comply with licence dormancy requirements”)
10. Not Operational: A licenced establishment is not open and temporarily ceased operating. In such instances,
the licence should be considered dormant. If an inspector believes that the licence in question is dormant
and is not listed as dormant in Dynamics, inspectors shall:
a. Go to the Licence view in Dynamics,

b. Under the Activities tab, add a task called “Dormancy Verification”, and
c. Assign that task to ‘CST liquor’
Staff from the Client Services Team (CST) will reach out and verify with the licensee that the licence is in
fact dormant, and update the licence in Dynamics as needed.
The inspector is to include what steps or observations have led them to determine the licence is not
operational. (i.e.: inspector notes a sign “out of business”) which would trigger licensing to send a
“Notice of Cancellation” letter, or the inspector notes a sign “closed for renos”) which indicates
dormancy. Licensing will follow up with an “Intent to Classify Licence as Dormant Notice” giving the
licensee two (2) weeks to provide a completed Dormancy Notification Form (LCRB100), or
If the establishment is currently operating, a written submission describing the current operations,
including hours of operation and in the case of a liquor licence, the details of any relevant information
such as recent liquor purchases and sales, stock levels, employee payroll, advertising etc.
11.
Operational: Where the establishment is identified as operational requires the inspector to create a
“Routine Inspection” and conduct the routine inspection at that time of attendance and in accordance with
established routine inspection procedures for that type of licence.
Inspectors shall conduct public safety inspections for each licence type in accordance with the procedures as
specified in the below sub-sections.

heading: 6.36 Public safety inspection of a FP/LP or manufacturing lounge
text:
Procedure:
1. Before entering the establishment, the inspector will conduct a site risk assessment to determine if it is safe
to conduct the inspection. The procedure for conducting a site risk assessment is specified within the C&E
Inspector Safety Manual. Prior to entering the establishment, the inspector will observe any advertising or
signs on the outside of the establishment,
2. The inspector will note the time and enter the establishment,
3. The inspector will make an initial observation of the establishment, including:
• activities at the door to screen identification, control the number of patrons in the
• establishment and control entry of intoxicated persons,
• the number of staff,
• the number of patrons,
• patron behaviour, and
• atmosphere,
4. If appropriate, the inspector will advise the licensee of the inspection,
29. If appropriate, the inspector will question the licensee on any previous concerns and what follow-up action
has been taken,
30. The inspector will make a critical observation of the patrons, entertainers, staff, and physical condition of
the establishment as the inspector moves through the establishment.

heading: 6.36 Public safety inspection of a FP/LP or manufacturing lounge
text:
The inspector will at minimum confirm
the licensee is in compliance with the following public safety requirements:
• Community Disturbance: the operation of the establishment is not disturbing the community,
• Disorderly or Unlawful Activities: there are no disorderly or unlawful activities occurring,
• Employee Consuming Liquor: licensee, management and staff are not consuming while working,
• Entertainment: there is no unauthorized entertainment or games occurring,
• Intoxication: intoxicated patrons or patrons showing signs of intoxication are not permitted entry or
are removed from the premises,
• Liquor Service: there is no over service and drink sizes and minimum pricing is adhered to,
• Minors: minors are not in attendance unless authorized and whether staff are consistently requesting
two pieces of identification when verifying that a patron is not a minor before serving them liquor,

• Operating Outside of Licence Purpose: in the case of a food primary that the primary focus of the
operation of the establishment is on the service of food,
• Overcrowding: the establishment does not exceed patron or person capacity or occupant load,
5. Items that the inspector should also be alert to during the inspection include:
• presence of weapons,
• liquor in unauthorized areas, and
• liquor promotions, contests or advertising that promotes or is likely to promote intoxication,
6. The inspector may conduct one or more formal counts of the number of patrons using a mechanical
counter to ensure the establishment is within the approved capacity, and
7.
The inspector may check identification of patrons to ensure patrons being served liquor are 19 years of age
or older. He/she may request that a staff member request the identification from patrons, as necessary.

heading: 6.37 Public safety inspection of a cannabis retail store or producer retail store
text:
Procedure:
1. Before entering the establishment, the inspector will conduct a site risk assessment to determine if it is safe
to conduct the inspection. The procedure for conducting a site risk assessment is specified within the C&E
Inspector Safety Manual,
2. Before entering the establishment, the inspector will observe:
• advertising or signs on the outside of the establishment meet requirements,
• activities occurring outside the establishment, e.g.: bootlegging for minors,
• whether intoxicated persons are entering or leaving the establishment, and
• Window displays to ensure compliance; externally directed displays containing cannabis or cannabis
accessories are prohibited
3. The inspector will note the time and enter the establishment,
4. The inspector will make an initial observation of the establishment, including:
• the number of staff,
• the number of patrons,
• patron behaviour, and
• atmosphere,
5. If appropriate, the inspector will advise the licensee of the inspection,
6. If appropriate, the inspector will question the licensee on any previous concerns and what follow-up action
has been taken,
7.

heading: 6.37 Public safety inspection of a cannabis retail store or producer retail store
text:
The inspector will observe and note the following:
• types of cannabis for sale, (i.e.: no unlawful cannabis and any non-medical cannabis sales meet
requirements),
• the presence of minors,
• unlawful activities,
• disorderly or riotous conduct,
• the presence of persons that are exhibiting the symptoms of intoxication from the influence of cannabis
or alcohol or another drug,
• presence of weapons,
• consumption of cannabis,
• unauthorized games or entertainment,
• there are no cannabis self-service options or vending machines, and
• there is no on-site consumption of cannabis
8. The inspector may check identification of patrons to ensure patrons being sold cannabis are 19 years of age
or older. He/she may request that a staff member request the identification from patrons, as necessary.

heading: 6.38 Public safety inspection of a LRS and a RLRS
text:
Procedure:

1. Before entering the establishment, the inspector will conduct a site risk assessment to determine if it is safe
to conduct the inspection. The procedure for conducting a site risk assessment is specified within the C&E
Inspector Safety Manual,
2. Before entering the establishment, the inspector will observe:
• advertising or signs on the outside of the establishment meet requirements,
• activities occurring outside the establishment, e.g.: bootlegging for minors,
• whether intoxicated persons are entering or leaving the establishment
3. The inspector will note the time and enter the establishment,
4. The inspector will make an initial observation of the establishment, including:
• the number of staff,
• the number of patrons,
• patron behaviour, and
• atmosphere,
5. If appropriate, the inspector will advise the licensee of the inspection,
6. If appropriate, the inspector will question the licensee on any previous concerns and what follow-up action
has been taken,
7. The inspector will observe and note the following:
• the presence of minors,
• unlawful activities,
• disorderly or riotous conduct,
• the presence of persons that are exhibiting the symptoms of intoxication from cannabis, alcohol, or
another drug, and
• presence of weapons,
8. The inspector may check identification of patrons to ensure patrons being sold cannabis are 19 years of age
or older. He/she may request that a staff member request the identification from patrons, as necessary.

heading: 6.39 Special Event Review and Risk Analysis
text:
General
LCRB’s compliance and enforcement role is limited to public safety considerations as they relate to the service
of liquor and ensuring compliance with the Act, Regulations and terms and conditions in the liquor service area.
Inspectors must focus on their mandate to regulate the Liquor Service Areas of Special Events and ensure the
T&Cs are being met. The branch should provide recommendations and guidance on permit requirements as they
relate to our role as the liquor regulator, not for the entirety of the event.

C&E Division will ensure compliance through “Risk Analysis.” Inspectors will inspect events when deemed
necessary to ensure the permittee is abiding by the Act, Regulations, and terms and conditions. By following the
“Risk Assessment” business process, inspectors will be in a better position to consistently identify high risk
events and allocate resources accordingly. Where a risk analysis deems it necessary, LCRB may ask for further
information to understand how liquor sales and service will be conducted to attendees.

heading: 6.40 Special event risk assessments and consideration for inspection
text:
Procedure:
1. The regional supervisor will routinely review all approved special event permits within the branch database
using the criteria established within the Risk Assessment Matrix to generate a report that reflects those
criteria,
2. The regional supervisor will then assign the approved special event permits to inspectors for review,
3. The inspector will review each special event using the Risk Assessment Matrix (see sub-section 6.42) and
make recommendation to the regional supervisor which events should be inspected,
4. The regional supervisor will finalize the list based on regional priorities and resources,
5. Upon approval by the regional supervisor to conduct an inspection of an SEP, the inspector will create the
inspection in the branch database.

determining which SEPs are to be considered for inspection.

heading: 6.43 Conduct of a special event inspection
text:
Procedure:
1. The inspector will review the branch database and confirm the Special event Permit has been issued for the
event requiring inspection,
31. The inspector will note the time and enter the event,
32. The inspector will identify themselves to the Permittee or representative and inform them of the intent of
the inspection.
2. If appropriate, the inspector will question the permittee on any previous concerns and what follow-up action
has been taken, and
3. The inspector will observe and note the following regarding the general operation of the event:
• Special Event Permit: ensure the Special Event Permit is posted for viewing within the liquor service
area,
• Event Permittee or Designate on Site: the permittee or designate must be onsite at all times during liquor
service hours,
• Site Plan: must be on site and accurately reflect the liquor service area,
• SIR/SES: all staff selling, serving, or supervising the sale of liquor have completed prescribed training,
• Liquor Service: drink sizes, pricing and liquor service hours adhered to and permittee/staff not consuming
liquor,
• Overcrowding: the permittee must not exceed the maximum attendance as specified on the permit or
occupancy load if applicable,
• Minors: ensure minors are not accessing or consuming liquor,
• Intoxication: ensure patrons are not intoxicated.

heading: 6.44 Conduct of a covert inspection
text:
Procedure:
1. One of the primary goals of the inspection and enforcement program is to increase compliance by licensees
through enforcement focused on key public safety issues, such as:
• intoxication,
• service to minors,
• overcrowding,
• unlawful liquor or cannabis,
• unlawful activities or disorderly conduct in licensed establishments, and
• liquor or cannabis related community disturbances associated with licensed establishments,
2. An effective method of ensuring success in identifying if any of the public safety issues specified above is
the utilization of inspections where the inspector covertly enters the establishment and presents
him/herself as a patron by requesting service in the form of food and/or alcohol purchase or cannabis
purchase and then observing and gathering evidence to determine non-compliance,

3. The execution of formal covert inspection planned operations as well as impromptu covert inspections
form part of a number of important tools branch inspectors have at their disposal to provide effective
“public safety,” regulatory oversight of both the liquor and cannabis industries, and
4. Inspectors may attempt to conduct a covert inspection in order to view the general management of an
establishment and the conduct of staff when they do not know they are being observed.

heading: 6.45 Impromptu covert inspections
text:
Procedure:
1. May be conducted at the discretion of the inspector absent a pre-approved operational plan where the
inspector:
• considers that an impromptu covert inspection is necessary to measure a licensee’s level of
compliance, and
• where the situation is a possible public safety urgency warranting the impromptu covert inspection and
immediate action by the inspector,
2. Impromptu covert inspections are to occur only where the inspector has reason to believe that a serious
public safety contravention possibly may be occurring or about to occur and for which the inspector
considers an impromptu covert is the best action to take in order to observe the contravention and/or
gather sufficient evidence, while adhering to the Risk Assessment that would normally be considered in
the “Covert Inspection Operational Plan”, and
3. Where an impromptu covert inspection has occurred, the inspector is to notify the Regional Supervisor
and/or Regional Manager by email of the impromptu covert inspection within 48 hours of the inspection
including the name and location of the establishment and the basis by which the inspector felt the
impromptu covert inspection was necessary.

heading: 6.46 Operationally planned covert inspections
text:
Procedure:
1. Must be pre-approved by the regional manager prior to execution. The primary intent of the operationally
planned covert inspection is to confirm non-compliance subsequent to the inspector having:
• previously conducted a recent compliance meeting with the licensee regarding alleged or proven non-
compliance, and
• subsequently received evidence or information to indicate the licensee continues to be in non-
compliance,
2. Operationally planned covert inspections generally may not be approved by the regional manager absent
the inspector having previously conducted a compliance meeting with the licensee regarding any previous
non-compliance findings or allegations,
3. Operationally planned covert inspections may be approved by the regional manager where the operational
plan is being carried out primarily as a method to measure industry compliance:
• during occasions such as community sporting events, special occasion licensed events or other times
where activities are occurring in a community and where there may be a higher risk to the public due
to the nature of the event, and/or,
• as a result of police LPC or other intelligence sources that indicate possible non-compliance by one or
more licensed establishments in one location,
4. Operationally planned covert inspections may be approved only where the inspection is conducted by an
inspection team consisting of at least two inspectors, and
5.
Where an inspector identifies a need to conduct an operationally planned covert inspection of a licensed
establishment, the inspector shall provide the regional manager with an operational plan (see “Covert
inspection operational plan format”) on how the covert inspection will be executed and at least 7 days in
advance of the anticipated execution date.

heading: 6.48 Expense Authority
text:
Regional Managers are the “Expense Authority” for approving expense claims and are responsible to ensure that
the covert liquor or cannabis expense is eligible and justified. As such, covert liquor or cannabis expense
purchases are authorized:
• where an inspector conducts an impromptu covert inspection,
• where an operationally planned covert inspection has been previously approved, and
• to the minimum extent necessary to gather evidence of a contravention, and to maintain the inspector’s
anonymity.

heading: 6.49 Purchasing and consumption during a covert inspection
text:
Liquor: Alcohol purchased during a covert inspection may be consumed only where it is necessary to maintain
the appearance of a customer including where an inspector conducts an impromptu inspection. Where
consumption is necessary the following restrictions apply:
• only one member of an inspection team may consume the purchased covert liquor. The other member of the
inspection team is to present themselves as the “designated driver” and purchase only a non-alcohol
beverage such as a soft drink or coffee,
• only part of the content of the purchased liquor may be consumed and only to the minimum extent

necessary to conduct the inspection,
• alcohol purchase is restricted to “the appropriate liquor” and to the circumstances of the venue, i.e. an
inspector would not purchase spirits where the purchase of a “low alcohol” beverage such as beer, wine or
wine cooler would be consistent with liquor being consumed by patrons in the establishment,
• avoid ordering of drinks that are served in clear glass containers, and
• utilize games such as darts and shuffleboard that may be present in the establishment to help the inspector
maintain covert capacity.

Cannabis: The consumption of cannabis inside a licensed cannabis retail store or producer retail store is
prohibited. LCRB inspectors shall not consume cannabis during any covert inspection including a covert
inspection to determine if the licensee is permitting consumption in the establishment.
Inspectors may purchase and consume food during a covert liquor inspection to:
• limit the effects of liquor consumption, and/or
• maintain the appearance of a customer.
Where a covert liquor or cannabis purchase expense occurs, the inspector must include within the “Justification”
comments section of the iExpense claim, the name of the covert or Minors as Agents Program (MAP) Operation
(if applicable) and the name of the licensed establishment where the liquor, food or cannabis was purchased.

heading: 6.52 Minors as Agents Program (MAP)
text:
MAP inspections are used to monitor compliance with legislative prohibitions against selling liquor or cannabis
to minors. Research shows that hiring minors is one of the most effective ways to monitor compliance with this
requirement. A MAP “Inspection Team” shall include a minimum of one trained minor agent, and at least a
minimum of two trained C&E Division staff [e.g.: Area Supervisor, Senior Inspector, liquor and cannabis
inspector and/or an investigator] or one liquor and cannabis inspector and one police officer who will
accompany and observe the minor agent at all times during the operation to ensure their safety and the integrity
of the inspection during the operation.

heading: 6.53 Minors as Agents Program (MAP) inspection team site selection and operational plans
text:
Procedure:
1. MAP inspections can be conducted at any establishment licensed under the LCLA or CCLA. Both
government liquor and cannabis retail stores can also be inspected; however, these inspections are subject
to an agreement with the Liquor Distribution Branch,
2. A MAP Inspection Plan will be completed by the Senior Inspector. It will be submitted to the Area
Supervisor for review and approval, no later than one full business day prior to the MAP operation.
3. Every MAP Inspection Plan will include:
• A list of the establishments to be inspected, their respective licence class and number, and indicate if
the inspection is Intelligence based or randomly selected,based on a high PIPER score, or is for
compliance verification.
a) Regarding Manufacturing Licenses: the specific endorsement (on-site store, lounge, or otherwise)
must be indicated on the Inspection Plan.
• Any unique safety considerations for branch staff and the minor agent and how those concerns will be
addressed (where applicable).
• Copies of each establishment floor plan.
4. The MAP Inspection plan must be assessed by the Senior Inspector as follows:
• Review of Dynamics Database for any establishment flags or noted safety concerns. The Senior
Inspector may consult with the local inspector to review the MAP Inspection Plan being conducted in
their area(s) of responsibility. The local inspector will inform of any known risks regarding the
licensee, staff, patrons, or environmental risks such as community dynamics, lighting, access, or

egress issues.

heading: 6.53 Minors as Agents Program (MAP) inspection team site selection and operational plans
text:
The local inspector may identify if two establishments/inspections are in plain view of
one another to avoid risk of detection between establishments and identifying minor agents.
• Where the local inspector or any member of the MAP inspection team including the minor agent, at
any time prior to or during the conduct of an inspection considers the minor agent to be at risk, the
inspection/operation shall be aborted and the inspection team will immediately inform the Area
Supervisor and/or Regional Manager of the context.
5. Establishments will be selected for inspection based on:
• “Intelligence” such as complaints, police information, observations made during previous inspections,
or other information that identifies an establishment as being high risk of sale to a minor, and
• “Random” where establishments are randomly selected and inspected consistent with the branch’s
public safety mandate to ensure responsible liquor service and cannabis sales, as well as delivering a
fair, impartial, and balanced regulatory program across both industries;
• “Compliance Verification” in instances wherein a licensee or permittee has been found non-compliant
with a MAP inspection within the previous 24 months;
• “PIPER” where establishments are identified as having:
o PIPER total risk scores of at least 1100, due to a formula of multiple risk variables identified
at the respective licence; and/or,
o PIPER public safety contravention scores of at least 800, due to multiple CNs identified at the
respective licence;

6.

heading: 6.53 Minors as Agents Program (MAP) inspection team site selection and operational plans
text:
A particular licensed establishment will generally not be inspected more than once on any particular shift
or operation, other than where the layout of the establishment (e.g.: an arena with numerous points of sale
or a special event with several service areas spread out through a location) warrants multiple testing as a
result.
7. Repeated testing of the same site over a short period of time is not permitted. However, subsequent MAP
inspections may occur where credible information pertaining to minors at that particular establishment is
received.
8. If the LCRB has received a complaint regarding services to minors and an investigation has been
assigned, multiple MAP inspections (no more than 2 in a 90-day period) may commence at the
establishment in an attempt to corroborate the information contained in the complaint file.
9. Establishments will not be “randomly” inspected more than once every 12 months unless a previous
contravention for non-compliance was identified, or for instances wherein specific Operational plans have
been developed for a specific establishment.
Where appropriate, the inspection team or the local inspector will advise local police of the presence of the
MAP inspection team in their community prior to the beginning of any operation.

heading: 6.55 Hiring of minor agents
text:
• The minimum age for agents is 16 years old. Where possible, the agent pool should have a gender balance
and reflect the cultural diversity of the geographic area where they will be working.
• Senior Inspectors will make a reasonable effort to maintain a pool of agents with year-round availability
to have consistent delivery of MAP inspections throughout the year.
• Direct relatives of branch staff may not be hired as minor agents; direct relatives are defined as birth-
children, step-children, adoptive-children, and grand-children of LCRB employees.

Minor Agent contracts and amendments
Hiring Minor agents and contract procurement will occur as follows:
• MAP applicants submit a resume and cover letter to lcrb.cande.admin@gov.bc.ca

respective region.
• The Senior Inspector will contact appropriate applicants to arrange an in-person or virtual interview.

• The applicant’s parent or guardian should be encouraged to attend the interview to be briefed on the
program and the expectations of minor agents.
• In-person interviews should always include a third-party to the Senior Inspector and the applicant; ie:
parent/guardian, secondary inspector, or area supervisor.
• If the applicant is deemed suitable for the position of minor agent, the Senior Inspector will complete and
submit a MAP General Service Agreement (GSA) contract to Lcrbaccounts@gov.bc.ca.
• The General Service Agreement (GSA) contract is to be signed by the minor agent, their parent/guardian,
and the LCRB C&E D

heading: 6.56 Safety and training of minor agents
text:
The LCRB “Safety First” policy applies to all MAP operations (Section 3.2 of the LCRB C&E Division Safety
Procedures Manual). Minor agents will participate fully in classroom training (complying with the Occupations
Health and Safety Regulation) before commencing field training or inspection activities.
• Minor agents must be instructed to comply with all verbal and non-verbal instructions regarding safety
during inspection or field activities.
• Minor agents must be instructed to never deviate from prescribed safety procedures.
• Minor agents must be instructed to leave the establishment immediately if required to do so by the
licensee’s staff or by the inspector, or if they feel threatened in any way.
• Minor agents must be instructed to report any safety related incident, near-miss situation, or perceived
danger to LCRB staff as soon as possible.

Inspection safety preparedness
The safety of the minor agent is the paramount concern. Therefore, the following procedures apply to all minor
agents and MAP inspections:
• Minor agents will not work in any area where their identity may be compromised. The determination of
risk is made by the inspection team.

heading: 6.56 Safety and training of minor agents
text:
The inspection team will not conduct an inspection where the minor
agent is at risk of identification or personal safety.
• Unless prior authorization has been confirmed by the Regional Manager in writing, the inspection team
will not conduct any MAP inspection past 11:00pm.
• Unless prior authorization has been confirmed by the Regional Manager in writing, the inspection team
will not conduct any MAP inspection within in a nightclub environment, nor where adult entertainment is
active.
• The MAP inspection team will conduct an on-site assessment prior to all inspections. Where there is any
risk, the inspection and/or the entire operation will be terminated.
• Agents must be visible to the inspection team at all times.
• At all times during the conduct of an operation/inspection the minor agent will be accompanied by, within
close proximity, or maintain a direct line of sight within the establishment by at least one inspector or
police officer.
• The inspection team will immediately advise the Regional Manager of any incident or altercation in
which a MAP inspection team member’s safety was compromised or where the situation escalated. If
necessary, in order to de-escalate an incident wherein safety may be compromised, an inspector will self

identify as a Liquor Inspector in an effort to de-escalate the situation. The minor agent(s) will be directed
to leave the establishment immediately and call 911 if necessary.

Reporting Minor Agent incidents
The risk of identifying a minor agent is significant.

heading: 6.56 Safety and training of minor agents
text:
This risk remains throughout the MAP process, from hiring to
inspections to attendance at any hearing and afterward. Minor agents will have these risks highlighted in training.
Never, for any reason, should a minor agent’s identity be compromised; therefore should any of the following
scenarios occur, the incident must be immediately reported to a Regional Manager, to the minor agent’s
parent/guardian, and potentially the police in applicable instances.
1. If the minor is identified as an agent by a patron or staff member at time of inspection.
2. The minor agent’s identity is revealed or otherwise inadvertently recognized.
3. Agents will not engage in confrontation or argue with establishment staff and will remove themselves
immediately if the situation becomes confrontational. If a confrontation occurs, the inspection team will
verbally intervene by self-identifying as a Liquor & Cannabis Inspector to establishment staff and escort
the minor agent safely from the situation and call 911 if necessary.
4. Where there is information that the licensee has retained CCTV of the minor agent, this matter will be
brought to the attention of the Director C&E Operations (i.e.: posting a picture behind desk or bar or on
social media).

heading: 6.58 Travel with minor agents
text:
• Minor agents will be picked up and returned to an agreed upon point of assembly. Minor agents may not
use their own vehicles during operations. All MAP operations will use government vehicles.
• Minor agents may be required to be away from home overnight to perform MAP operations. If travel is
required overnight a Minor Agent must be accompanied by an adult supervisor following the MAP shift.
This supervisor must be the Minor Agent’s parent, guardian, stepparent, grandparent, or another adult
(approved by the guardian and Regional Manager in writing) who could reasonably be expected to act in
place of a parent and to be responsible for supervision of the minor.
• The adult supervisor may not be involved in any manner with the inspections.
• The adult supervisor will receive reimbursement any incurred mileage at the flat government rates via the
minor agent’s contract. Mileage can be claimed for travel directly associated with traveling to and from
their home address and the destined accommodation, as well as any additional business mileage, travel
tolls incurred, and parking expenses with transaction receipt.
• The minor agent and adult supervisor will be granted appropriate accommodation as coordinated and paid
by an LCRB employee via LCRB operational budget.

heading: 6.58 Travel with minor agents
text:
Minor agents are never permitted to share
accommodation with an LCRB employee.

• No other reimbursements will occur for the adult supervisor.

proceed with travel (ie: airfare, ferry) and accommodation bookings for the minor agent and their adult

3. Minor agents may be required to testify at administrative hearings.
Purchased product will be logged as evidence. Reference section 9 of this manual for further information.

heading: 6.61 Post-Minors as Agents Program (MAP) inspection contact with the licensee
text:
1. If no products are sold to the minor agent, the Branch will email liquor and cannabis licensees within 14
days after MAP inspections to notify them that they've passed a MAP inspection. These emails are
automatic templated emails in Dynamics, to which licensees will not be able to respond. If a licensee has
follow-up questions, they can contact their LCRB inspector or email LCRB.CandE.Admin@gov.bc.ca.

Only licensees who refuse service to minor agents will receive these notifications. Licensees who sell
liquor or cannabis to a minor agent will be contacted by their LCRB inspector.

2. If products are sold to the minor agent, all evidence is to be documented during and after the inspection and
all related forms are to be completed by the minor agent and/or inspector.
3. If products are sold to the minor agent, an Electronic Notification of Non-Compliance is to be issued as
soon as practicable after the documentation is completed and the minor is safe. Notification must be sent as
soon as practicable to ensure administrative fairness to the licensee as well as to minimize the risk of future
sale of liquor or cannabis to a minor.
4. The safety of the minor agent is paramount. Non-compliance may be raised with a licensee at a later time
where a risk to the issuing inspector or to the minor agent has been identified and can be documented.
5. Subsequent enforcement action will be determined pursuant to “Issuing an Electronic Notification of Non-
Compliance.”
A penalty proposal will generally be made for non-compliance identified by a MAP inspection. The branch`s
normal enforcement process will then be followed pursuant to Section 12 of the LCRB C&E Operational
Procedures Manual: "The Enforcement Process.”
1. Inspection teams will enter complete inspection results on each branch database establishment file, and
2. Inspection teams are responsible for gathering evidence, documenting the inspection, entering data into the
branch database, issuing the Electronic Notification of Non-Compliance and any enforcement action that
may flow from the inspection.

heading: 6.64 Conduct of a Minors as Agents Program (MAP) inspection
text:
These procedures are guidelines for use by liquor and cannabis inspectors. Each inspection will prove to be different
based on size/layout/sightlines within the establishment, the nature and number of staff and patrons. Inspectors are
expected to continuously analyze these environmental factors throughout the entire inspection. If at any point during
the inspection, an Agent or Inspector declares the inspection unsafe, these procedures can be modified to ensure the
safety of the Agent(s), the Inspector(s), and the public.

1. Pre-MAP Operation:
• Ensure the inspection plan has been reviewed by the Regional Supervisor and local area Inspector.
• Inspectors will ensure they have printed or have access to electronic copies of all applicable MAP forms
and documents prepared for the operation.
• Inspectors will obtain a sufficient amount of petty cash necessary to conduct the inspection plan.
• Inspectors will ensure the government vehicle has a sufficient amount of fuel, is equipped with all
safety and emergency supplies, and that the SafetyAware App or InReach device is fully functional and
checked in prior to the MAP operation.
• Prior to the MAP shift, Inspectors will communicate with the Agents regarding the date and time to
begin the MAP shift, the point of assembly, and the expected shift conclusion time.

heading: 6.64 Conduct of a Minors as Agents Program (MAP) inspection
text:
At the Point of Assembly:
• Photograph the Agent(s): a full body shot and headshot are taken of the Agent using a Government
issued computer, iPhone, or iPad. These photographs are to be initialed and dated by the Agent and an
Inspector, either physically or electronically.
• The Agent will provide 2 pieces of identification, which must contain their age and DOB (ID issued by
a government agency and a secondary ID with the Agent’s signature and or picture). The identification
is to be photographed using a Government computer, iPhone, or iPad and initialled and dated by the
Agent and an Inspector.
• An inspection plan briefing will be held before each operation begins with an emphasis on safety, and
a review of the establishments identified for inspection.
• The Inspectors and Agent(s) will exchange cell phone numbers for the purposes of communication
throughout the shift.
• Inspectors will ensure the Agent provides an emergency contact number for a designated person
available for the entirety of the operation. Inspectors are encouraged to communicate with the
emergency contact to notify basic information of the shift; includi ng anticipated start/end times, pick
up/drop off location, and community of operations.
• When communicating with the Agent, Inspector’s are to refer to the Agent using their Agent # only.
• Electronic Copies of Minor Agent photographs and identification must not be entered into Dynamics.

3. Upon Arrival at the Establishment:
• The government vehicle will be parked as close to the establishment as possible.

heading: 6.64 Conduct of a Minors as Agents Program (MAP) inspection
text:
If possible, the
government vehicle should not be in direct view of the establishment. The government vehicle must
attempt to avoid obvious locations that could draw attention to the MAP inspection team.
• The area is scanned for any potential problems/threats to the safety of the Agent or inspection team. If
any real or perceived threats are identified, the inspection will be abandoned . If the inspection team
determines the conditions are appropriate, the inspection will proceed.
• A single inspector is to enter the establishment or event, assess and position themself separately but
within adequate observation distance from the Agent, and maintain a consistent line of site of the Agent
upon their entrance and for the entire inspection. Preferably, the inspector will be positioned where the
liquor/cannabis transaction can be clearly observed, whilst avoiding obvious locations which might
draw attention to the inspector.
• The floor plan or event site plan (if available) will be reviewed with the Agent(s) to identify the entry
and exit points of the establishment or event . Service areas, points of sale, and drink ticket purchases
area (if applicable) should also be identified and highlighted to the Agent.
O If the site plan is unavailable for an SEP, the Inspectors will first gain access to the event to
observe entrance and exit points and advise the Agent of those locations.

heading: 6.64 Conduct of a Minors as Agents Program (MAP) inspection
text:
An emergency
meeting point will be established between the Inspector team and the Ag ent, both within and
outside the Event.
• Agent(s) and Inspectors note time and location in their respective notes.
• The Agent is issued funds for the attempted liquor/cannabis purchase; the Agent must not use their own
debit or credit card to make a purchase.
• The Agent leaves their identification in the vehicle to ensure they are not placed in the position of
having to lie when asked whether they have identification. The Agent is reminded not to lie or deceive
to achieve the sale of liquor/cannabis. THERE ARE NO EXCEPTIONS.
• One inspector will remain in the vehicle to maintain line of sight of the Agent entering and exiting the
establishment and receive/seize any product purchased.
• If at any time, an Inspector(s) or Agent(s) believe the establishment to be unsafe for any reason,
the inspection will be immediately aborted.
• The Agents and Inspectors must abide by any signage or obvious protocols instructed by the licensee
or establishment; i.e.: “Please wait to be seated ; Please remain in ticket and identification cue ; Please
see host or hostess prior to entrance.” All establishment-instructed protocols must be adhered to.

4.

heading: 6.64 Conduct of a Minors as Agents Program (MAP) inspection
text:
Entry of the Establishment and Execution of Inspections
• Agent(s) and Inspectors record time of entry into their respective notes.
• One inspector will remain in the vehicle to maintain line of sight of the Agent entering and exiting the
establishment and receive/seize any product purchased.
• One Inspector will enter the establishment prior to the Agent to conduct a dynamic risk assessment of
the establishment to ensure the safety and security of the Minor Agent(s).
• If during the risk assessment, the Inspector recognizes any variable that would compromise the
inspection or the safety and security of the Agent and/or Inspectors, the inspection will be aborted. This
includes the collection of patron names or any other personal identifiers.
• If there are no recognizable concerns, the Inspector within the establishment will contact the secondary
Inspector in the transport vehicle to confirm it is appropriate for the Agent(s) to attend the
establishment.
• The Agent(s) will walk directly to the establishment and will make efforts to maintain line of sight for
the secondary Inspector to ensure the Agent safely reaches the establishment.
• Upon entry of the Agent, if approached by a security or door staff for identification, the Agent will
advise that they do not have identification.

heading: 6.64 Conduct of a Minors as Agents Program (MAP) inspection
text:
If requested by the security or door staff, the Agent will
exit and return immediately to the transport vehicle.
• If at any time during the inspection, the Agent is asked for their name or any other personal identifier,
the Agent will politely refuse the request, exit the establishment, and return immediately to the transport
vehicle.
• The Branch recognizes that each license class requires its own unique procedures; therefore, please see
the MAP Procedures Appendix (at the end of the manual) for detailed protocols of each respective
license class.
• These procedures may vary as circumstances dictate within an inspection to ensure the safety of the
Agent, Inspector(s), and the public is maintained.

5. Post-Inspection:
• Upon exiting the establishment with (or without) purchased product, the Agent must return directly to the
government vehicle.
• An Inspector will seize the liquor/cannabis product and retain the sales receipt if available.
• Once the secondary Inspector has returned to the government vehicle, the inspection team will relocate to
another location reasonably distant from the establishment.
• If the Agent was able to purchase liquor/cannabis, an exhibit sticker is placed on the seized product where
appropriate, completed with time, date, location, exhibit number, and initialed by the Inspector.

heading: 6.64 Conduct of a Minors as Agents Program (MAP) inspection
text:
All fields
on the exhibit bag are to be filled out by an Inspector.
• The Agent completes the Observation Form.
• An Inspector reviews the Observation Form for accuracy prior to the Agent and Inspector signing the report.
• The Agent then completes the Minor Agent Observation & Statement form to include:
▪ Inspection information
▪ Inspection results & product description
▪ Server/Sales Associate details
▪ Observations from entry to exit.
▪ Recollection any conversation with the staff, as specific as they can recall.
▪ Description of the staff, with as many details about the staff as possible.
▪ If identification was requested . Agents will make note of the context in which they were
asked for ID.
• An Inspector reviews the Minor Agent Statement for accuracy prior to the Agent and Inspector signing the
document.
• Both Inspectors document their entire involvement and observations, to include:
▪ Establishment name and license number.

▪ Date, time of entry, and exit of the establishment.
▪ Description(s) of the staff and names if available.
▪ Type, volume, and name of product.
▪ If a request for identification was heard by the Inspector.
• Deposit all the completed documents in an envelope for safe keeping.
• If safe and appropriate to do so, an inspector may re -enter the establishment to notify the
licensee/establishment manager/LDB manager of the alleged contravention. The Inspector will instruct the
manager to notify the licensee of the contravention if the licensee is not present.

heading: 6.64 Conduct of a Minors as Agents Program (MAP) inspection
text:
The Inspector will request
the Selling/Serving-It-Right certificate of the sales clerk, personal government ID of the sales clerk, and

• Electronic copies of Agent(s) photographs of their person from before and after the shift, and photographs
