This section of the manual is designed to assist participants in the enforcement hearing process by outlining roles
and responsibilities, branch policies, procedures for scheduling and conducting pre-hearing conferences and
enforcement hearings.

heading: 43.1 Enforcement Hearing
text:
The Enforcement Hearing Process assists the branch’s registrar, the case management administrator, registrar,
branch advocates and enforcement hearing delegates in performing their roles within the enforcement hearing
process. The role of the inspector in the enforcement hearing process is also described in this process. This
information is here only to provide background to the enforcement hearing process and to allow for the accurate
representation of the workflow during the process. As a result, some of the procedures or information contained in
this manual duplicate or reference information provided elsewhere in this manual.

The enforcement hearing processes is guided by “Role of the Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch” and
“Administrative Law Principles.” Decisions of the enforcement hearing delegate are guided by the policy
statements for each type of contravention as well as general branch policies with respect to determining penalties
and penalty imposition dates outlined in “Enforcement Hearing Rules.”
There are several principles that guide the enforcement hearing process. Readers should reference the following
references within the C&E Operational Procedures Manual:
• “Role of the Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch”
• “Operating assumptions of the Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch,” and
• “Administrative Law Principles.”

heading: 43.3 Relationship to other compliance and enforcement processes
text:
It is important to remember that the enforcement hearing process is one part of the larger Compliance and
Enforcement Program of the branch. In order to place enforcement hearings in their appropriate context within the
Compliance and Enforcement Program, a number of other branch processes are referred to in the following
sections. The following is a brief description of these processes and how they intersect with the enforcement
hearing process.

heading: 43.4 Notice of Enforcement Action (NOEA)
text:
If a liquor and cannabis inspector identify a contravention to the Liquor Control and Licensing Act (LCLA) or the
Cannabis Control and Licensing Act (CCLA), and related regulations or the terms and conditions of the licence,
authorization or permit, the inspector may recommend an enforcement action. If the branch proceeds, the
licensee/permittee will be issued a NOEA letter. The issuance of the signed NOEA against the licensee begins the
enforcement hearing process. The NOEA is sent to the Case Management Administrator (CMA) through the
branch database to initiate case tracking.
Upon receipt of the NOEA, the licensee/permittee can either sign a waiver accepting the penalty or request an
enforcement hearing. The licensee or permittee can sign a waiver notice from receipt of the NOEA up until the
time the hearing is set to begin. Once the hearing begins, the licensee or permittee loses the option to sign a
waiver.

heading: 43.6 Pre-hearing conference (PHC) and hearing
text:
If a licensee/permittee does not sign a waiver, the CMA will schedule a pre-hearing conference. A notice of the
PHC will be issued, which outlines the options available to the licensee/permittee when responding the NOEA.
Generally, the licensee will be invited to attend a PHC within 14 days from the date of the NOEA.
During the pre-hearing conference, the registrar, among others, will determine whether the response of the
licensee/permittee to the allegations necessitates the holding of an enforcement hearing.
Hearings may be written or oral and an oral hearing may be conducted in-person or remotely. If an oral hearing is
to be held, the registrar will confirm the date and location of the enforcement hearing with all participants, via a
letter, fax, or email.
At the enforcement hearing, the licensee/permittee may assert that the alleged contravention(s) did not occur,
and/or the proposed enforcement action is not warranted. The hearing delegate will consider both the
licensee/permittee and the Branch’s evidence and argument and issue a written decision within 30 days from the
conclusion of the hearing.
43.7 Case Management Administrator
The Case Management Administrator (CMA) is responsible for providing administrative support to the registrar
and the hearing delegate, scheduling hearings and pre-hearing conferences, and tracking the progress of each case
ensuring all information is entered into the content management system and decisions are posted to the branch
website.

heading: 43.6 Pre-hearing conference (PHC) and hearing
text:
As well, the CMA is responsible for distributing reports, decisions, and letters on behalf of the registrar
and the enforcement hearing delegate.

The CMA answers procedural questions from licensees or branch staff regarding the enforcement hearing rules or
enforcement hearing process. The CMA does not provide information to licensees or permittees or inspectors
regarding substantive issues such as the sufficiency of evidence, or the content of notices of enforcement action.

heading: 43.8 Enforcement Hearing Registrar
text:
The Registrar, Enforcement Hearings is responsible for developing and managing the branch's enforcement
hearing process. The registrar ensures the hearing process is administratively fair, complies with the governing
legislation, and contributes to the soundness and integrity of the general manager's statutory decision-making.

Reporting directly to the general manager, the registrar is responsible for independently managing all aspects of
the branch's enforcement hearing program and must ensure that it provides a fair and efficient process to all
participants involved.

The registrar develops monitors and evaluates policies, procedures, enforcement, and hearing activity in order to
support the general manager and branch in carrying out its mandate.

heading: 43.9 Enforcement Hearing Delegate
text:
The general manager has delegated to the hearing delegate authority under section 5 of the LCLA and section 5 of
the CCLA to adjudicate at enforcement hearings. At the enforcement hearing, the hearing delegate is acting under
the authority of the general manager and with all the powers of the general manager in an enforcement hearing.
Once a hearing delegate is assigned to a case, the assigned hearing delegate is the only person delegated the
authority to decide the case.

At an enforcement hearing, the hearing delegate will:
• determine whether a contravention occurred,
• determine what penalty, if any, to impose, and
• determine any matter related to the penalty such as the date a suspension commences or the number of days
within which a monetary penalty must be paid.

While the general manager has delegated their authority to the hearing delegates, the general manager retains
authority to take action under sections 51 to 53 of the LCLA and sections 38 and 39 of the CCLA. The delegation

of the authority to the hearing delegates does not exhaust the authority of the general manager to act under those
sections. This means that the general manager continues to have authority to adjudicate enforcement hearings.
However, for the sake of clarity within this manual, the term ‘hearing delegate’ has been used in place of the term
‘general manager.’

heading: 43.10 Branch Advocate
text:
The branch advocate is responsible for representing the branch at pre-hearing conferences and enforcement
hearing proceedings.

In advance of the enforcement hearing, the Branch advocate:
• identifies and prepares the Branch’s witnesses for hearings,
• gathers, reviews, and discloses all relevant documents and information to the licensee/permittee and prepares
the Branch’s argument,
• reviews documents for privacy concerns and redacts photos and identification of minor agents,
• determines any need for further investigation and clarification of evidence, and
• prepares submissions for oral presentation. If the hearing is on written submissions, the advocate prepares
written submissions for presentation to the hearing delegate.

If the branch advocate has concerns regarding the branch evidence and representations, the branch advocate
should consult with the responsible regional manager. If the branch advocate finds that there is no sufficient
evidence to establish the alleged contravention, the branch advocate may recommend to the deputy general
manager to discontinue the enforcement action.

During the enforcement hearing, the branch advocate will present the branch’s evidence regarding enforcement
action.

heading: 43.10 Branch Advocate
text:
This will include:
• examining branch witnesses,
• cross-examining licensee/permittee witnesses,
• presenting the proposed penalty from the NOEA for an alleged contravention and the rationale for the
proposed penalty,
• presenting the rationale for taking enforcement action, including a discussion of branch policy and the public
interest, and
• presenting the process and standards the branch follows to provide information to the licensee/permittee and
how that process was applied to the licensee/permittee in question.

If the licensee/permittee fails to attend a scheduled hearing after due notice, the branch advocate may make
submission to the hearing delegate to proceed with the hearing of the branch’s evidence and present the branch’s
evidence in the absence of the licensee/permittee.

The branch advocate also plays a role in preparation of the enforcement hearing record in the case of
reconsideration or judicial review, and may assist the branch solicitor with preparation for, and attendance at
judicial review proceedings.

The branch advocate is responsible for maintaining a library of case precedents and reviewing enforcement
hearing, reconsideration, and court decisions for implications on branch policy and procedures. The branch
advocate will also research precedents from other jurisdictions. The branch advocate also works with branch staff
and other enforcement agencies to develop consistency in the standard of evidence presented at enforcement
hearings.

heading: 43.11 Licensee/Permittee and Licensee’s/Permittee’s Representative
text:
During the enforcement process the licensee/permittee may appoint another person to represent the
licensee/permittee’s position on an alleged contravention and proposed penalty. The representative of the
licensee/permittee may be legal counsel, or some other person appointed by the licensee/permittee.

The licensee/permittee and/or their representative are expected to attend at any pre-hearing conferences and at the
enforcement hearing. When the licensee/permittee or their representative does not participate in the pre-hearing
conference, the registrar decides whether to set the matter for a written hearing, or to take other appropriate steps.
If the licensee/permittee does not participate in the enforcement hearing, it is the decision of the hearing delegate
whether or not to proceed. The licensee/permittee is responsible for meeting the disclosure requirements outlined
in the enforcement hearing rules, and for organizing and ensuring attendance of their own witnesses.

heading: 43.12 Liquor and Cannabis Inspector
text:
In general, the role of the liquor and cannabis inspector during the enforcement hearing process includes:
• preparing and facilitating the signing of the waiver notice upon consent of the licensee/permitted and
notifying the CMA, advocate, and the registrar to discontinue the process if a waiver notice is signed,
• if no waiver is signed, assisting the advocate by providing information, and evidence, relating to the NOEA
issued, and
• attending the enforcement hearing as a witness for the branch and testifying about the alleged contravention,
the reasons for pursuing a particular enforcement action and any prior compliance activity related to the
licence or the licensee.

When attending an enforcement hearing as a branch witness, the inspector will familiarize themselves with the
file history for the licensee and establishment in question and be prepared to give evidence concerning prior
contraventions, warnings, police Licence Premise Checks (LPC’s), local government and community concerns
and any other documentation or information relevant to the hearing. In some situations, the advocate and the
inspector’s regional manager may request that the inspector obtain further evidence, prior to the matter proceeding
to the enforcement hearing.

heading: 44.0 Introduction
text:
The enforcement hearing rules are distributed to licensees with the notice of enforcement action. The rules are
also available on the branch website. The rules were designed to assist licensees/permittees in understanding the
enforcement hearing process and to ensure a consistent approach to enforcement hearings. The registrar will
answer questions from licensees/permittees regarding enforcement rules and procedures.

The enforcement hearing rules are branch policy. As a result, the hearing delegate may exercise discretion when
imposing these rules in order to ensure administrative fairness in all situations. The full text of the rules is
reproduced below.

heading: 44.1 The Enforcement Program
text:
The role of the Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch (the “branch”) enforcement program is to ensure that all
licensees/permittees comply with:
• the Liquor Control and Licensing Act (LCLA),
• the Liquor Control and Licensing Regulation (LCLR),
• the Cannabis Control and Licensing Act (CCLA),
• the Cannabis Licensing Regulation (CLR), and
• with the terms and conditions of their applicable licence/permit.

While the goal of the branch is to minimize infractions through education and voluntary compliance, enforcement
action may be necessary when there is a serious contravention or repeated contraventions of the Acts, regulations
and/or with the terms and conditions of a licence/permit.

It is important for the branch to act against noncompliance to promote public safety and interest. A delay in
dealing with noncompliance or the absence of a response to noncompliance may endanger the public or
compromise community standards. As well, it may encourage further incidences of noncompliance.

heading: 44.2 The Authority of the General Manager
text:
Sections 51 to 53 of the LCLA and sections 38 and 39 of the CCLA authorizes the general manager of the
branch, with or without a hearing, to act against a licensee/permittee for alleged contraventions of the applicable
Act, regulations and/or the terms and conditions of the licence or permit. The general manager may take one or
more of the following enforcement actions:
• impose a term and condition on a licence or permit or rescind or amend existing terms and conditions,
• impose a monetary penalty,
• impose a suspension of the liquor or cannabis licence for a time,
• cancel all or part of a liquor or cannabis licence or permit, and
• order a licensee to transfer a licence.

heading: 44.3 The Enforcement Hearing Delegate
text:
The general manager’s authority under sections 51, 52 and 53 of the LCLA and sections 38, 39 and 40 of the
CCLA has been delegated to enforcement hearing delegates. Although the general manager retains the authority
to chair enforcement hearings, in general, most enforcement hearings will be chaired by an enforcement hearing
delegate of the general manager. This means that the enforcement hearing delegate will hold an enforcement
hearing; consider the evidence of the branch and the licensee or permittee at the enforcement hearing; decide
whether a contravention has occurred; and what enforcement action, if any, to impose.

heading: 44.4 The Enforcement Process
text:
A Notice of Enforcement Action will be sent to the licensee notifying the licensee/permittee that enforcement
action may be taken for an alleged contravention(s) of the LCLA/CCLA or associated regulations or the terms and
conditions of the licence, permit or authorization. The NOEA will include a statement of the alleged

contravention(s), the proposed enforcement action, and the facts on which the alleged contravention(s) and
proposed enforcement action are based.

When the licensee/permittee receives a NOEA, the licensee/permittee may sign a Waiver Notice. Signing a
Waiver Notice means that the licensee/permittee:
• agrees that the licensee/permittee has committed the contravention(s),
• accepts the enforcement action(s) proposed in the NOEA,
• waives the opportunity to an enforcement hearing on the matter,
• waives the right to request reconsideration of the findings of the contravention(s) and the enforcement
action(s), and
• agrees that the finding(s) of contravention and the specified enforcement action(s) will form part of the
compliance history of the licensee/permittee.

If a licensee/permittee does not sign a Waiver Notice, the registrar may convene an enforcement hearing. Prior to
the enforcement hearing, the registrar may require the licensee/permittee to attend a pre-hearing conference with
the branch advocate.

heading: 44.4 The Enforcement Process
text:
At a pre-hearing, the registrar may:
• provide information to the licensee regarding the enforcement hearing process and the allegations
• identify, clarify, and narrow the issues in dispute,
• discuss the evidence that will be presented,
• set out the requirements for the disclosure of evidence between the branch and the licensee/permittee,
• determine whether an enforcement hearing is required and if so, in what format,
• discuss date(s) and time for the hearing and witness availability, and
• set out procedures to ensure a timely, fair, and efficient hearing.

At the enforcement hearing, the licensee/permittee may argue that:
• a contravention did not occur,
• a proposed penalty is too severe, and/or
• the licensee was duly diligent in preventing the contravention.

If more than one contravention is alleged, the licensee/permittee may agree to one contravention but make
representations regarding the other contraventions and the proposed penalties.

The hearing delegate aims to issue a written decision within 30 days after the hearing is concluded. If a penalty is
imposed, the branch will carry out the imposition of the penalty.

If the licensee or permittee is dissatisfied with an enforcement order, they may apply within 30 days for
reconsideration.

heading: 44.5 The Penalty Schedule
text:
Schedule 2 to the LCLR and Schedule 2 to the CLR establishes the Enforcement Actions Penalty Schedules (the
“penalty schedules”) which sets out the suspension and monetary penalty ranges for a contravention.

Note: An amended penalty schedule of the Liquor Control and Licensing Regulation came into effect on June 5,
2019, and applied to contraventions arising after the new penalty schedule has taken effect.

If the enforcement hearing delegate finds that a contravention has occurred and that a licence suspension or a
monetary penalty is warranted, the enforcement hearing delegate is bound by the minimum penalties in the
penalty schedule. The enforcement hearing delegate has discretion to impose penalties greater than those set out
in the penalty schedule.

heading: 44.6 The Enforcement Hearing Rules
text:
The following rules are the practices the branch will follow in preparing for and in conducting an enforcement
hearing.

Rule 1 - Purpose of rules
The purposes of these Rules are:
• to assist licensees and permittees in understanding the enforcement hearing process,
• to ensure a consistent approach in enforcement hearings, and
• to ensure the timely, fair, and efficient adjudication of alleged contraventions.

Rule 2 - Application
These Rules replace the previous Rules and apply to all cases effective May 31, 2021.

Rule 3 - Definitions
In these rules:

“Act(s)” means the Liquor Control and Licensing Act, and/or the Cannabis Control and Licensing Act, as
amended from time to time,

“Branch” and “LCRB” means the Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch,

“Branch advocate” means the person appointed by the general manager of the Branch to represent the Branch at
enforcement proceedings,

“case management administrator” or “CMA” means the case management administrator of the branch,

“contravention” means an act or omission that is contrary to the provision(s) of the Act(s), their Regulations,
and/or a failure to comply with a licence term and condition: “cannabis contravention” means a contravention of
the Cannabis Control and Licensing Act, Regulations and non-medical cannabis licence terms and conditions,

“liquor contravention “means a contravention of the Liquor Control and Licensing Act, Regulations and liquor
license terms and conditions,

“enforcement order” means an order made imposing a penalty after a finding of either a liquor or non-medical
cannabis contravention:

heading: 44.6 The Enforcement Hearing Rules
text:
“section 51 order” is an enforcement order issued under the Liquor Control and Licensing Act,

“compliance order” is an enforcement order issued under the Cannabis Control and Licensing Act,

“expert report" or "expert evidence" means evidence expressing an opinion based on education, training, or
experience,

“hearing delegate” means the general manager of the Branch and any person to whom the general manager has
delegated their powers, duties and functions under the Acts and Regulations for the purpose of conducting and
adjudicating enforcement hearings,

“licensee” means licensee as defined in the Acts; and in these Rules, a licensee also refers to a licensee’s
representative or a permittee,

“permittee” means a permittee as defined by the Liquor Control and Licensing Act,

“produce” refers to the provision of a document or other evidence on which either the Branch or a licensee, third-
party, or their representative(s) intends to rely at a hearing. These documents or evidence must be provided by
mail, courier, fax transmission, or email and received at the addressee’s address for delivery as required under the
Acts or Regulations, or as directed by the hearing delegate or registrar, as the case may be,

“registrar” means the person to whom the general manager of the Branch has delegated their powers, duties and
functions under the Act and Regulations for the purpose of facilitating pre- and post-hearing proceedings,

“Regulation(s)” means the Liquor Control and Licensing Regulation or the Cannabis Licensing Regulation or the
Cannabis Control Regulation.

heading: 44.6 The Enforcement Hearing Rules
text:
“Rules” means these enforcement hearing rules,

“Waiver Notice” or “waiver” means a notice in form and content satisfactory to the general manager, by which
the licensee expressly and irrevocably:
• agrees that the licensee committed the contravention,
• accepts the enforcement action proposed in the Notice of Enforcement Action (“NOEA”),
• waives the opportunity to have an enforcement hearing on the matter; and
• agrees that the finding of contravention(s) and the penalty(ies) will form part of the compliance history of the
licensee.

Rule 4 - Extension or Reduction of Time
At any time, the hearing delegate or registrar, as the case may be, may extend or reduce the time for an application
or the performance of any obligation under the Rules as long as it does not alter any time limits set out in the Act
or Regulations.

Rule 5 - Representation
The licensee may be self-represented, represented by legal counsel or represented by any person who has written
authority to act for the licensee, throughout the enforcement process, including representation at the hearing.

Rule 6 - Waiver
The licensee may sign a waiver at any time from receipt of the NOEA, up until the time the hearing is set to
begin.

The licensee may waive the opportunity for an enforcement hearing for one or more of the contraventions alleged
in the NOEA. The enforcement hearing process will continue for any contraventions that have not been waived.

Rule 7 - Oral or Written Hearing
1.

heading: 44.6 The Enforcement Hearing Rules
text:
If the licensee does not sign a waiver, the registrar will set a date for an oral hearing or timelines for written
submissions, as applicable. The registrar will make reasonable efforts to accommodate the Branch and
licensee’s scheduling requirements.

2. For an oral hearing, the Branch will send out a written notice of hearing, by mail or email.

Rule 8 - Rescheduling before the Hearing Date
1. The registrar may reschedule a hearing on their initiative, or in exceptional circumstances.

2. If either the Branch or the licensee seeks to reschedule the hearing, they must apply by letter or email, which
must be received by the registrar at least 14 days before the hearing and must say why they are asking to have
the hearing rescheduled, keeping in mind that the registrar will only reschedule if there are exceptional
circumstances.

3. If a hearing is rescheduled, the registrar may set any terms respecting further rescheduling, production of
documents or reports, or other matters which may assist with the timely, fair, and efficient conduct of the
hearing.

4. The registrar may set any terms and conditions respecting scheduling, attendance at pre-hearing conferences,
production of documents, or any other matters which may assist with the timely, fair, and efficient conduct of
the rescheduled hearing.

Rule 9 - Pre-hearing Disclosure
1. The branch advocate and the licensee shall produce to each other copies of anything they intend to submit as
evidence at the hearing at least 14 days before the hearing unless the registrar orders otherwise.

2.

heading: 44.6 The Enforcement Hearing Rules
text:
The branch advocate and the licensees must produce their witness lists containing the names of their witnesses
and roles or positions at least 14 days before the hearing date unless the registrar orders otherwise.

3. The branch advocate and the licensee must produce a copy of any expert report(s) that they intend to submit as
evidence at the hearing, at least 21 days before the first day of the hearing, unless otherwise ordered by the
registrar. If either the branch advocate or the licensee intends to call an expert witness without a report, they
must produce a written statement of the opinion to be given, the facts upon which the opinion is based and the
qualifications of the expert witness at least 21 days before the first day of the hearing, unless otherwise ordered
by the registrar.

Rule 10 - Pre-hearing Conference (PHC)
1. The registrar may set guidelines or direction for the timely, fair, and efficient conduct of a hearing, including
the convening of a PHC.

2. The registrar may direct that a PHC be held in person, by telephone conference or by some other method and
set directions relating to videoconference proceedings.

3. At a PHC, the registrar may:
a. provide information to the licensee regarding the enforcement hearing process and the allegations,

b. assist in clarifying, identifying, and narrowing the issues in dispute,

c. determine the enforcement hearing format, as set out in Rule 7,

d. discuss the evidence (including witnesses) that will be presented at the enforcement hearing,

e.

heading: 44.6 The Enforcement Hearing Rules
text:
set out the requirements for the pre-hearing disclosure of evidence, including expert evidence and agreed
statement of facts, if any, between the branch advocate and the licensee,

f. require the branch advocate and the licensee to prepare and produce a list of witnesses and a written
summary of a witness’ evidence, without a report, that party must produce a written statement of the opinion to
be given, the facts upon which the opinion is based and the qualification of the expert witness,

g. discuss and set locations, date(s), and time for the enforcement hearing, and in doing so may consider
witness’ availability,

h. issue summons for witnesses, if required,

i. set deadlines and directions in case of a penalty-only written submissions,

j. determine if the licensee or witnesses requires any services to attend the hearing, such as for example, access
for persons with disabilities, interpretive services, or services for the deaf,

k. impose time limitations and terms and conditions on the production of documents, expert reports, agreed
statement of facts, written submissions, or any other processes necessary for the fair and efficient management
of the hearing,

l. set out procedures to ensure a timely, fair, and efficient hearing.

4. By letter sent by mail, email or fax, the registrar will report the results of the PHC to the branch advocate and
the licensee, including a summary of the issues and any orders or directions from the registrar made during the
PHC.

Rule 11 - Hearing Procedures
1.

heading: 44.6 The Enforcement Hearing Rules
text:
This Rule applies to oral hearings, whether held in person or by videoconference. Hearings relating only to
penalty generally proceed by way of written submissions.

2. Unless authorized by the registrar, no hearing participant shall forward or share the invitation or hyperlink
sent to them for the hearing by videoconference. All participants must comply with the directions relating to
videoconference proceedings provided by the registrar prior to the hearing or as set by the hearing delegate at
the hearing.

3. If the licensee does not attend the hearing, the hearing delegate may proceed or adjourn the hearing to a later
date.

4. The Branch does not record enforcement hearings.

5. The hearing delegate may establish their own practices and procedures for the conduct of the hearing and
may:
a. determine the procedures for the hearing,
b. make determinations regarding the admissibility of evidence,
c. require the production of evidence,
d. proceed in the absence of the licensee or witness or in the absence of any submissions from the licensee
when the licensee has had notice of the proceeding,
e. ask questions to clarify issues or facts,
f. place time limitations on the examination or cross-examination of witnesses or presentation of opening or
closing submissions,
g. require presentation of written submission, and/or
h. adjourn a hearing.

Rule 12 - Adjournments
1. Once the hearing has commenced, the hearing delegate may adjourn a hearing on their own initiative or at the
request of the branch advocate or the licensee.

2.

heading: 44.6 The Enforcement Hearing Rules
text:
In case of technical difficulties occurring during a hearing by videoconference, the hearing delegate may
adjourn the hearing where appropriate and practical.

3. The hearing delegate will only grant an application for adjournment of a hearing if exceptional circumstances
justify the adjournment.

4. In determining whether to grant an adjournment the hearing delegate may consider, but is not limited to, the
following factors:
a. the reasons for the request and any objections by the branch advocate or the licensee to the adjournment,

b. the number of rescheduled hearings and adjournments that have already been granted,

c. whether the adjournment will needlessly delay or impede the conduct of the hearing,

d. whether the purpose for which adjournment is sought will contribute to the resolution of the matter,

e. whether the adjournment is required to ensure a fair opportunity to be heard,

f. the degree to which the need for the adjournment arises out of intentional actions or the neglect of the
applicant, and

g. matters of public health and safety

heading: 44.7 Reconsideration and Judicial Review
text:
1. If the licensee is dissatisfied with the hearing decision, they may apply to the general manager for a
reconsideration within 30 days after the date on which the order was received.
2. The applicant must complete and sign the application for reconsideration forms prescribed by the branch:
• For Liquor - LCRB Form 126
• For Non-medical Cannabis - LCRB Form 136

The official versions of the forms are accessible from the branch’s website. The applicant must include within the
form or in a separate paper a written submission identifying how they meet the grounds for reconsideration.

heading: 44.8 Request for extension of time
text:
If the licensee wishes to apply for a reconsideration after the lapse of the 30-day deadline, the licensee must
complete “Part 2- Request for Extension” of the Application for Reconsideration form, together with the
application for reconsideration.
44.9 Judicial Review
If a licensee is not satisfied with a reconsideration order, they may apply for judicial review within 30 days of
receiving the reconsideration order pursuant to the Judicial Review Procedure Act [R.S.B.C. 1996, c241]
Administrative fairness requires that the branch disclose to the licensee/permittee all documents that are relevant
to the allegations in issue, whether or not they assist the branch. This section provides guidance on the disclosure
process.
This section establishes the case management procedures.
The inspector will follow the procedures outlined in “The Enforcement Process” in order to prepare and
distribute the NOEA.

heading: 45.3 Initiating case tracking
text:
The Case Management Administrator (CMA) will receive an electronic copy of the NOEA in the branch database
from the inspector. If necessary, the CMA will remove the appendices from the electronic version of the NOEA.
The CMA will save an electronic copy of the NOEA without appendices in a case folder. The licence, legal entity
and contact information along with the NOEA is saved in the case folder and printed for the file. The prehearing
conference is then scheduled with the licensee, registrar, and branch advocate.

heading: 45.4 Reviewing the NOEA and determining the availability of witnesses
text:
The branch advocate will review the NOEA, appendices and attachments received from the inspector.

The branch advocate will contact the branch witnesses to determine their availability for an enforcement hearing.
Where police witnesses are involved, the branch advocate may fax the relevant detachment or municipal force and
request confirmation by return fax of police officer availability (see sub-section 46.4 for sample fax of a Law
Enforcement Notification (LEN)). Wherever possible, but particularly in the case of large detachments or
municipal forces, the branch advocate will determine the process used by crown counsel for scheduling police
witnesses and mimic the process if acceptable to the police agency.

The branch advocate will provide the registrar with information regarding the availability of branch witnesses for
an enforcement hearing at the time of scheduling the pre-hearing conference.
If the licensee/permittee contacts the inspector in order to sign a waiver, the inspector will follow the procedures
outlined in “Waiver Notice” to prepare the waiver, obtain the licensee/permittee’s signature, and distribute signed
copies of the waiver. If a hearing has been scheduled, the inspector will inform the CMA, branch advocate and the
registrar to discontinue the process.
If a waiver is signed, compliance and enforcement headquarters will follow the procedures outlined in “Imposing
Penalties” to impose the penalty.
If the CMA receives a copy of the signed waiver from the inspector, the CMA will create the penalty letter and
signs for the DGM’s signature and then distribute. The information is entered on the All NOEAs excel
spreadsheet and tracked in the branch database until the monetary penalty is paid in full or suspension served.
The CMA will track the file in the branch database and move forward with scheduling the prehearing conference
after the date the NOEA is issued.

heading: 45.9 Scheduling the pre-hearing conference
text:
If the CMA does not receive a copy of the signed waiver notice, the CMA will schedule a pre-hearing conference.
The enforcement hearing process continues within the established time frames until such time as the CMA
receives a signed copy of the waiver notice. If at any point in the process the licensee/permittee indicates to the
CMA that they wish to sign a waiver, the CMA will direct the licensee/permittee to contact the inspector to have
the waiver notice completed and signed and will notify the branch registrar and advocate by e-mail

The CMA will open an electronic case folder and working paper file for the case.

The CMA will determine the branch advocate responsible for the case. The CMA will schedule the one-hour
prehearing telephone conference with the registrar and advocate ensuring they are both available.

The CMA will contact the licensee by email or telephone and inform them that a pre-hearing conference is being
scheduled. The CMA will confirm the licensee contact name, telephone and fax contact number, and whether the
licensee/permittee will be represented by counsel. The CMA will note on the working file the name and contact
information for the licensee/permittee’s representative. Any letters sent to the licensee/permittee will also be
provided to their representative.

The CMA will prepare a notice of pre-hearing conference letter (see sample“Pre-hearing Conference
Confirmation Letter”), sign the letter and distribute by outlook meeting request along with the NOEA and liquor
licence.
The meeting invite is sent to the registrar and branch advocate with a copy to the liquor inspector. The
licensee/representative will be informed by email and the signed original sent to them by mail. A copy is placed in
the electronic and working paper file.

The CMA will indicate in the “All NOEAs” excel spreadsheet and branch database the date set for the pre-hearing
conference.
The branch advocate prepares a binder or bound copy of the disclosure documents to be presented at the hearing.
The branch advocate prepares an enforcement hearing submission to be presented orally at the hearing, or to be
presented in written form during written submissions.
These enforcement hearing procedures are divided into the four main stages of the hearing process:
• the waiver period,
• the pre-hearing period,
• the enforcement hearing period, and
• and the reconsideration period.

Each of these stages is represented by a flow chart followed by a text description of the procedures undertaken at
each step indicated on the flow chart.

heading: 45.12 The waiver period
text:
The CMA begins case tracking as soon as the NOEA is received. However, the CMA does not begin scheduling a
pre-hearing conference and an enforcement hearing for the case unless the licensee fails to sign a waiver
following the issuance of the NOEA.

The procedures outlined in steps 1 to 10 in the below flow chart:
• ensure the enforcement action is tracked and that staff are aware of how to proceed in the event a waiver is
signed, and
• ensure the commencement of the pre-hearing process in the event a waiver is not signed.

The policy relating to waiver notices is set out in “Waiver Notice.” Two policies that have particular relevance to
the enforcement hearing process are:
• the licensee/permittee may waive the opportunity to an enforcement hearing for one or more of the
contraventions listed in the NOEA. The enforcement hearing process continues for any contraventions that
have not been the subject of a waiver notice, and
• the licensee/permittee may sign a waiver notice at any time up to the commencement of the enforcement
hearing. If the CMA receives a signed copy of the waiver notice, the enforcement hearing process for those
contraventions is discontinued.

A pre-hearing conference provides an opportunity for the registrar to set procedures for the efficient conduct of
the enforcement hearing.

heading: 45.14 Procedures for the pre-hearing period
text:
The procedures for pre-hearing conferences are set out in the enforcement hearing rules.
More than one pre-hearing conference may be required for a particular case.

The procedures outlined below:
• ensure that the results of the pre-hearing conference are shared with all participants,
• ensure that disclosure requirements outlined in the enforcement hearing rules or by the hearing delegate
during the pre-hearing conference are satisfied in advance of the enforcement hearing,
• ensure that any requests for rescheduling of the enforcement hearing are considered in accordance with the
policy outlined in the enforcement hearing rules,
• ensure that the branch is prepared administratively for the conduct of the enforcement hearing, recording of
the hearing and management of exhibits, and
• ensure that the branch advocate and branch witnesses are prepared to present evidence at the enforcement
hearing.
The CMA will communicate a request for rescheduling of a pre-hearing conference to the registrar and the non-
requesting licensee or advocate and document the request by placing it in the working file.
The registrar will decide whether the rescheduling should be granted. The registrar may contact the
licensee/permittee and/or licensee/permittee’s representative and/or the branch advocate in determining whether
to grant the rescheduling request.

The registrar will communicate the decision on the rescheduling request to the CMA.
The registrar or the CMA will communicate the decision on a rescheduling request to the branch advocate and the
licensee/permittee and/or the licensee/permittee’s representative.

The CMA will document the decision on the working file.

heading: 45.18 Scheduling another pre-hearing conference
text:
If a request to reschedule the pre-hearing conference is granted or if another pre-hearing conference is required,
the registrar or CMA will schedule another pre-hearing conference.

If a time for the pre-hearing conference has not already been determined, the CMA will contact the registrar,
branch advocate and the licensee/ representative to determine a convenient time for the pre-hearing conference.

The CMA will schedule the prehearing telephone conference.

The CMA will prepare a notice of pre-hearing conference letter (see sample “Pre-hearing Conference
Confirmation Letter”), sign the letter and distribute by outlook meeting request along with the NOEA and liquor
licence to the registrar and branch advocate with a copy to the liquor inspector. The licensee/representative will be
informed by email and the signed original sent by mail. A copy is placed in the electronic and working paper file.

The CMA will indicate in the branch database and the All NOEAs excel spreadsheet the date set for the pre-
hearing conference.

heading: 45.19 Conducting a pre-hearing conference and scheduling the enforcement hearing
text:
The licensee/permittee and or licensee/permittee’s representative, registrar and the branch advocate will
participate in the pre-hearing conference. The CMA does not participate in the pre-hearing conference but will
contact the participants in order to inform them of contact information if necessary.

If anyone does not participate in the pre-hearing conference call, the registrar may decide to continue with the pre-
hearing conference in their absence or ask the CMA to reschedule the pre-hearing conference.

The registrar will set the date, length of time, and location for the enforcement hearing after conferring with the
participants in the pre-hearing conference.

heading: 45.20 Adjourning a pre-hearing conference
text:
The registrar may decide to postpone or adjourn the pre-hearing conference or determine that there is a need to
have another pre-hearing conference. The registrar will attempt to schedule the next pre-hearing conference
during the conference call with the participants.

If determined, the registrar will e-mail the CMA the details of the date and time for the reconvened or next pre-
hearing conference.

The registrar will schedule another pre-hearing conference.

heading: 45.21 Preparing a pre-hearing conference report
text:
The registrar will prepare a written report after each pre-hearing conference and forward to the case management
administrator for distribution. The registrar may decide to postpone preparation of the pre-hearing conference
report until after any additional pre-hearing conferences for the case have occurred. The report includes the
following information:
• any rulings or directions made at the pre-hearing conference,
• any requirements for disclosure made at the pre-hearing conference,
• whether the licensee/permittee has made a request for branch records pursuant to freedom of information
legislation (if known),
• the date and time determined for the enforcement hearing, and
• procedures for requests for rescheduling or postponement of the enforcement hearing.

heading: 45.22 Booking a location for the enforcement hearing
text:
The registrar will inform the CMA of the date and location where the enforcement hearing will be held. The CMA
will then confirm a boardroom, using provincial or federal government facilities, and send out a notice of hearing
letter with the details to all participants. All case materials (Notice of hearing, reporting out letter, NOEA and
licence) are then sent by mail to the hearing delegate assigned to the case.

The CMA will record the hearing date in the branch database and the All NOEAs excel spreadsheet.

heading: 45.23 Confirming that disclosure requirements were met
text:
The advocate will copy the registrar and the CMA on disclosure of documents to the licensee to ensure they are
both informed that disclosure requirements have been met. The advocate will inform the registrar of any reasons
why some or all disclosure cannot be made within the required time frame and may request an extension of time.
Licensees/permittees may similarly request an extension of time, or the advocate and licensee/permittee may
discuss disclosure delays directly between themselves and be prepared to raise any disclosure issues with the
hearing delegate.

heading: 45.24 Disclosing documents and information to the licensee/permittee
text:
The branch advocate will review the disclosure requirements outlined by the registrar in the pre-hearing
conference report.

The branch advocate will send by email or registered mail any documents, information and expert reports or
opinions to the licensee/permittee in accordance with the requirements outlined in the pre-hearing conference
report, branch policy and the enforcement hearing rules (see sample “Cover letter for Disclosure of Documents”).
If the licensee/permittee attends at the branch advocate’s office in order to obtain the documents, the branch
advocate will ask the licensee/permittee to indicate receipt of the documents by signing the cover letter.

heading: 45.25 Preparing branch witnesses
text:
As soon as possible after the date and location of the enforcement hearing is confirmed, the branch advocate will
notify branch witnesses of the date, time, and location of the enforcement hearing. The branch advocate will
email, fax, or mail a notice to each witness outlining the date, time, and location of the enforcement hearing. The
branch advocate will communicate to the CMA any special needs that must be accommodated for witnesses (e.g.:
disabled access, interpretive services, services for the deaf).

The branch advocate will review evidence with branch witnesses and prepare them for questioning and cross-
examination at the enforcement hearing.

heading: 45.26 Finalizing the pre-hearing preparations
text:
The branch advocate will:
• evaluate the completeness of the evidence to be presented and determine whether further evidence is
required,
• prepare the branch representations for the hearing,
• prepare a book of authorities and make copies for distribution at the hearing,
• organize all exhibits and make copies for distribution at the hearing, and
• arrange for their own travel and accommodation for the hearing

The enforcement hearing rules set out the powers of the registrar and the hearing delegate to order production of
documents by the licensee/permittee and the timelines for disclosure of documents and expert opinions or reports
in advance of the enforcement hearing.
The following procedures detail the procedures for the enforcement hearing.
Request for rescheduling of the enforcement hearing must be addressed to the registrar for consideration.
The registrar will decide on the request based on the criteria outlined in the enforcement hearing rules. The
registrar may prepare a written decision responding to the application request and forward the decision to the
CMA for distribution.

heading: 45.31 Rescheduling the enforcement hearing
text:
If a request for rescheduling is granted, or a hearing delegate requests a rescheduling or adjournment of the
hearing, the registrar will schedule another hearing.

The CMA will prepare a further notice of enforcement hearing letter and distribute to all participants either via
email or mail and a copy to be placed on the working file.

The CMA will record the hearing date in the branch database and on the “All NOEAs” excel spreadsheet.

heading: 45.32 Informing branch witnesses of the rescheduled hearing date
text:
The branch advocate will notify branch witnesses of the date, time, and location of the rescheduled enforcement
hearing. If time allows, the branch advocate will email, fax, or mail a notice to each witness outlining the date,
time, and location of the enforcement hearing (see sample notice letter). Alternatively, the branch advocate may
contact the branch witnesses by telephone to inform them of the hearing date.
45.33 Conducting the enforcement hearing
The hearing delegate, branch advocate, licensee/permittee, licensee/permittee’s representative and witnesses for
the branch and licensee/permittee will participate in the enforcement hearing.

The hearing delegate conducts the hearing in accordance with the enforcement hearing rules.

heading: 45.34 Adjourning the enforcement hearing
text:
Where a hearing is adjourned, the hearing delegate will attempt to reach consensus on a new hearing date and
time while the participants are present.

The case number remains the same for the reconvened hearing.

The CMA will book a location for the hearing and notify hearing participants of the time and location for the re-
adjourned hearing.

The advocate will inform any branch witnesses required of the re-adjourned hearing date, either by telephone or a
faxed or emailed notice to witness.
Within 30 days from the completion of the hearing, the hearing delegate will issue a written decision and forward
to the registrar for review.

heading: 45.36 Determining penalties
text:
Where the hearing delegate finds that a contravention occurred, and enforcement action should result, the hearing
delegate will generally follow branch policy when determining the appropriate penalty, unless exercising their
discretion in unusual circumstances.

If the hearing delegate finds during an enforcement hearing that a penalty should be imposed for more than one
contravention of the same type, the hearing delegate will not consider the earlier contravention as a proved
contravention when determining the appropriate penalty range for the second contravention. A contravention may
only be considered as a second or subsequent contravention in accordance with Schedule 2 of the LCLR,
Schedule 2 to the CLR or the Schedule to the WQR if it was committed after the date upon which either:
• the licensee agreed to the earlier contravention by signing a waiver notice, and
• the general manager or hearing delegate decided that the earlier contravention occurred.

In general, the date for imposition of a penalty will be set at approximately 6 weeks from the date of the
enforcement hearing decision. This time frame allows for the reconsideration period and time for the
reconsideration delegate to review an application for reconsideration.

Orders for transfer of a licence will specify that the transfer must be approved by the general manager and
completed to a person at ‘arm’s length’ from the licensee. The enforcement hearing decision will generally
suspend the licence pending the completion of the transfer and allow the licensee 90 days within which to
complete the transfer.

heading: 45.36 Determining penalties
text:
In general, the enforcement hearing decision will direct that the licence be cancelled if the
transfer is not completed within the specified time period.

If the hearing delegate determines that a licensee or permittee has contravened the LCLA, CCLA or associated
regulations and/or the terms and conditions of its licence, permit or authorization, the hearing delegate may take

no enforcement action, or pursuant to section 51(2) of the LCLA or section 38 of the CCLA, may take one or
more of the following actions:
• impose terms and conditions on the licence or rescind or amend existing terms and conditions,
• impose a monetary penalty on the licensee,
• suspend all or any part of the licence,
• cancel all or any part of the licence, and
• order the licensee to transfer the licence.

The hearing delegate is not bound to order the penalty proposed in the NOEA. However, if the hearing delegate
finds that either a licence suspension or a monetary penalty is warranted, the hearing delegate is bound to follow
the minimums set out in Schedule 2 of the LCLR and Schedule 2 to the CLR but is not bound by the maximums
and may impose higher penalties when it is in the public interest to do so.

heading: 45.37 Distributing the enforcement hearing decision
text:
The CMA will receive the decision from the registrar, format, review and distribute. A signed copy goes to the
licensee/representative with copies to the branch staff and one for the establishment file. The decision is then sent
to the branch FOI coordinator for review prior to being posting to the branch website.

The CMA will record on the ALL NOEAs excel spreadsheet and the branch database the date of the decision and
penalty imposed.

The CMA will retain the case file and exhibits for 30 days from the date of the decision in case a reconsideration
application is filed.
This final stage of the enforcement hearing process encompasses the time period from the distribution of the
enforcement hearing decision until the final conclusion of any applications for reconsideration and/or judicial
review.
Reconsideration allows a licensee or permittee to have enforcement orders reviewed without having to apply to
the court for judicial review, as long as the application for reconsideration meets the prescribed grounds.
Reconsideration is a prerequisite for judicial review.

heading: 45.40 Grounds for reconsideration
text:
A licensee or permittee may apply for reconsideration if the application meets one of the prescribed grounds:
• there is new, substantial, and material evidence that was not available at the time of the original hearing,
• there was an error of law, and
• there was a failure to observe the rules of procedural fairness

These are the only reasons that a decision may be reconsidered. Reconsideration is not an opportunity to re-argue
the case. Licensee or permittees have 30 days from the date they are served with an enforcement order to apply in
writing to the general manager for reconsideration. The general manager may extend the deadline if special
circumstances prevent the licensee from meeting the deadline.

heading: 45.41 Application process
text:
A licensee or permittee must submit the application form, a $500 application fee and a written submission
identifying how they meet the grounds for reconsideration. The application fee will only be refunded if the
enforcement order is rescinded in the reconsideration order. If an application for reconsideration is accepted,
the licensee or permittee will be notified in writing that the penalty will be stayed until the reconsideration
decision has been received by them. If an application for reconsideration is rejected, a letter will be sent to
explain the reason for the decision. The letter will also confirm the penalty and may provide a new date of
payment or service of suspension.

The general manager will delegate reconsideration decisions to a hearing delegate. The enforcement order may be
upheld, varied, or rescinded. Once a decision is reached, the reconsideration order will be sent to the licensee or
permittee with a letter that will set out any further details with respect to the decision.

heading: 45.42 Judicial Review
text:
If the licensee or permittee is not satisfied with a reconsideration order, they may apply for judicial review within
30 days of receiving the reconsideration order pursuant to the Judicial Review Procedure Act [R.S.B.C. 1996], c.
241.
45.43 Procedures for the reconsideration period
The following details the procedures for the reconsideration period

The application for reconsideration will be received by the CMA to be forwarded to the Registrar. The Registrar
will review the application for completeness/timeliness (applicant form, fee, and date received). The Registrar
may issue stay of penalty, if required to provide time to adequately make a decision on rejection or acceptance of
the application.

The Registrar will determine whether the application satisfied the requirements of section 53.1(5) of the LCLA or
section 40(5) of the CCLA. If it does not, the application cannot be accepted.

The Registrar will send a written notice to the applicant of whether the application was accepted or rejected.

If the application is accepted, the Registrar will assign the reconsideration application to a new hearing delegate.
The CMA, with the assistance of the branch advocate, will copy all exhibits and logs for the case and send a
tabbed package of the materials and a covering letter to the hearing delegate outlining the contents of the package.

The hearing delegate will determine that an oral hearing is required. If so, the applicant will be notified of the
hearing date, time, and location.

The applicant will receive a copy of the reconsideration order.
Compliance and enforcement headquarters will receive a copy of the enforcement hearing decision and, if a
penalty is determined; will follow the procedures outlined in “Imposing Penalties” to impose the penalty.

heading: 45.45 Reviewing the enforcement hearing decision
text:
The branch advocate will receive a copy of the enforcement hearing decision and will review the decision for
potential impact on branch policy and procedure. Where the branch advocate finds any impact, the branch
advocate will prepare a briefing note or recommendations for a change in policy or procedure for review and
follow up by the DGM Compliance and Enforcement.

The branch advocate will schedule a review of the file for 30 days from the date of the enforcement hearing
decision.
The CMA will receive all stamped exhibits files from the hearing delegates after completion of the enforcement
hearing. The files are kept onsite until the reconsideration period for the case has expired.
The CMA will review the file at the end of the 30-day reconsideration period and determine whether or not
reconsideration has been filed.

The CMA will indicate in the branch database and on the “All NOEAs” excel spreadsheet whether
reconsideration was filed. If no reconsideration application is received, then the files are box listed and sent offsite
as per the filing retention schedule.
If reconsideration is filed, the CMA, with the assistance of the branch advocate, will copy all exhibits and logs for
the case, and send a tabbed package of the materials and a covering letter to the hearing delegate outlining the
contents of the package.
The CMA will record in the “ALL NOEAs” excel spreadsheet and the branch database the file status. The CMA
will close the working file and transfer all documents, onto the headquarters establishment file.

heading: 45.50 Reviewing the reconsideration decision
text:
The branch advocate will receive a copy of the hearing delegate’s reconsideration decision and will review the
decision for potential impact on branch policy and procedure. If the branch advocate finds any impact, the branch
advocate will prepare a briefing note or recommendations for a change in policy or procedure for review and
follow up by the DGM Compliance and Enforcement.

The advocate will file a copy of the reconsideration decision in their precedent file.

45.51 Scheduling a review of the file at the expiry of the judicial review application period
If the decision of the original hearing delegate is upheld upon reconsideration, the branch advocate will schedule a
review of the file 30 days after the date of the reconsideration decision.

heading: 45.52 Reviewing the file 30 days after the date of the reconsideration decision
text:
The branch advocate will review the file 30 days after the date of the reconsideration decision.
If no application for judicial review is filed, the branch advocate will close their working file for the case. If an
application for judicial review is filed, the hearing delegate and branch advocate will follow the procedures
outlined above for reconsiderations, in order to prepare for and represent the branch at judicial review
proceedings.

45.53 Deciding how to proceed if the reconsideration decision is not upheld on Judicial Review
The DGM Compliance and Enforcement, with the assistance of the registrar, hearing delegate and the branch
advocate if required, will decide how to proceed in the event the hearing delegate’s reconsideration decision is not
upheld on Judicial Review.

heading: 45.54 Reinitiating or abandoning enforcement action
text:
If the decision is made to reinitiate enforcement action, compliance and enforcement headquarters will reinitiate
enforcement action against the licensee/permittee, with regard to the findings of the Judicial Review.

If the decision is made to abandon enforcement action, compliance and enforcement headquarters will follow the
procedures outlined in “Discontinuing the Enforcement Process” to alert the licensee/permittee, other agencies,
and other branch staff of the decision.

heading: 45.54 Filing an application for appeal of judicial review
text:
If the decision is made to appeal the judicial review, the branch solicitor, with the assistance of the branch
advocate or hearing delegate if required, will prepare, and file an application for appeal of the judicial review. The
branch solicitor and branch advocate will follow the procedures outlined above for reconsiderations, in order to
prepare for and represent the branch at a judicial review proceeding.

heading: 46.1 Sample Pre-hearing Conference Confirmation Letter

[Date]

[Licensee Name and Address]

Dear [Sir/Madame] :

Re: [Legal Entity/Establishment/LP Number, Case Number]
The branch has recently sent you a Notice of Enforcement Action (NOEA) letter which explains the branch’s
reasons for pursuing enforcement action, the alleged contravention(s), and proposed penalty(s).

Next Steps

I have set a pre-hearing conference to discuss the above noted enforcement action. The Branch Registrar,
[Name], will conduct the pre-hearing conference by way of telephone conference call. The assigned Branch
Advocate will also participate.

I have attached to this letter a list of pre-hearing conference discussion topics and a copy of Enforcement Hearing
Rule #11. Please come to the pre-hearing conference prepared to discuss the topics outlined.

The pre-hearing conference will only be postponed in exceptional circumstances. A request for rescheduling must
be received before the pre-hearing conference date.

If you fail to participate in the pre-hearing conference, you may lose your opportunity for an oral hearing. In that

enforcement action.

Options

There are three options available to you in response to this enforcement action.

thoroughly review and understand your options.

Option #1 - waiver

A waiver includes all of the following elements:
• The licensee agrees that the contravention occurred as alleged in the NOEA
• The licensee accepts the proposed enforcement action (penalty) outlined in the NOEA
• The licensee agrees that the contravention and enforcement action will form part of the compliance history of

• The licensee waives the opportunity for an enforcement hearing
The pre-hearing conference will take place on:
[Date/Time] Pacific Time

A waiver can be signed for any or all of the contraventions alleged in the NOEA.

Option #2 – written submissions hearing

A penalty-only written submissions hearing includes all of the following elements:

• The licensee admits that it contravened as alleged in the NOEA
• The licensee is not pursuing a due diligence defence to the contravention
• The licensee only disputes the proposed enforcement action (penalty)

If you select the written submissions (penalty-only) hearing option, you will still need to participate in the
scheduled pre-hearing conference wherein the branch registrar will provide you with further details on the
process.

Option #3 – oral hearing

heading: 47.0 Introduction
text:
Under section 19(1) of the Liquor Control and Licensing Act (the Act), the General Manager is prohibited from
issuing, renewing, or transferring a licence to an applicant who may not be deemed fit and proper. At any time
during the term of a licence, the General Manager may, on their own initiative, determine whether a licensee is fit
and proper to hold or retain a licence. The General Manager also has the authority to take action against a licensee
who is not fit and proper. The Act and regulations provide little direction to the General Manager on how to apply
or exercise these authorities. Branch policy guides the General Manager in determining whether or not an
applicant or licensee is fit and proper and the procedures that branch staff follow to assist the General Manager in
making this determination.
A fit and proper investigation is conducted by an investigator who collects information that is relevant to a
determination of whether an applicant or licensee is fit and proper to hold a licence. At the conclusion of the
investigation, the investigator recommends whether the applicant or licensee is fit and proper. Fit and proper
investigations may be initiated as the General Manager deems necessary and may be commenced at any time
during the term of a licence.

heading: 47.0 Introduction
text:
A fit and proper investigation may be initiated where:
• the results of a fit and proper assessment on a new application indicate concerns and the application is referred
for an investigation by Licensing staff,
• a licence application requires automatic referral for a fit and proper investigation, or
• Branch staff identify fit and proper concerns relating to an existing licensee and the investigation is referred to
the Deputy General Manager of Compliance and Enforcement for approval.

heading: 47.1 Roles and responsibilities
text:
A number of branch staff have a role in fit and proper assessments, investigations and determinations as described
below
47.2 Branch Investigators
Investigators have been appointed as Special Provincial Constables under the Police Act. Investigators have
limited police officer authority for the purpose of maintaining the preservation of public peace by ensuring the
collection of intelligence will prevent criminals and persons associated with criminal activity from obtaining or
holding a liquor licence in the province. Investigators are responsible for:
• conducting fit and proper investigations of applicants and licensees,
• documenting the results of fit and proper investigations,
• presenting fit and proper concerns regarding existing licensees to the Provincial Director Compliance and
Enforcement for a decision whether a fit and proper investigation is required, and
• sharing information and intelligence with law enforcement and other regulatory agencies.

heading: 47.3 Licensing Case Managers
text:
Licensing case managers review and process licensing applications. Case managers are responsible for:
• conducting fit and proper assessments of applications,
• referring applications for fit and proper investigations, and
• updating information in the branch database as applications move through the fit and proper process.

In the case of applications other than new liquor primary licence applications, some of these tasks will be
performed by the case manager’s supervisor.
Licensing managers are responsible for:
• reviewing and approving requests for fit and proper investigations where an application does not require
automatic referral or where a licensing staff member identifies fit and proper concerns regarding an existing
licensee, and
• ensuring implementation of fit and proper determinations.
The Manager of IPCAT is responsible for reviewing fit and proper concerns brought forward to the Branch and
determining whether an investigation is required. he Manager IPCAT is also responsible for assigning fit and
proper investigations to investigators, providing direction and oversight into the conduct of an investigation, and
reviewing the investigators’ work and reports.
Both the Provincial Directors C&E and Licensing Operations are jointly responsible for reviewing staff reports of
fit and proper investigations and determining if the reports should be forwarded to the General Manager for
determination.
The registrar performs similar tasks to those performed during the enforcement process. The registrar is
responsible for:
• disclosing staff reports to the applicant or licensee, and
• arranging and facilitating the hearing process.
The registrar performs these responsibilities with the assistance of the case management administrator.

heading: 47.8 General Manager and Delegates
text:
The General Manager and Delegates are responsible for making determinations of whether an applicant or
licensee is a fit and proper person. If the General Manager or Delegate finds that an existing licensee is not fit and
proper, the general manager or delegate will also determine the appropriate action. If the fit and proper
determination relates to an applicant, licensing authority rests with the DGM Licensing.

heading: 47.9 Management Services staff
text:
Management Services staff are responsible for processing licence renewal applications. Licensing clerical staff are
responsible for ensuring that any licence renewal processed during a fit and proper investigation of an existing
licensee is only for the term recommended by the responsible investigator. Where the renewal term of an existing
licence is changed, systems services staff are responsible for making the appropriate change on the Branch
database.

ASSESSMENTS AND INVESTIGATIONS

heading: 48.0 Introduction
text:
A fit and proper assessment is an assessment conducted by licensing staff to determine if there are any concerns
regarding whether an applicant is fit and proper. This assessment is performed as part of the licensing process for
all new licence and licence transfer applications, as well as those types of licence amendments that introduce a
new person who may have control over the operation of the establishment.
Generally, the assessment involves a review of the documentation provided with the licence application. In some
cases, licensing staff may ask the applicant for further information as part of the assessment. Where the results of
the fit and proper assessment indicate fit and proper concerns, or where the licence application meets the criteria
for automatic referral, licensing staff will refer the application for a fit and proper investigation. If there are no fit
and proper concerns resulting from the assessment and the application does not require automatic referral,
licensing staff will continue with the licensing process.
A fit and proper investigation is conducted by a branch investigator to collect information that is relevant to a
determination of whether an applicant or licensee is fit and proper. At the conclusion of the investigation, the
investigator decides whether the information collected supports an allegation that the applicant or licensee is not
fit and proper.

heading: 48.0 Introduction
text:
Fit and proper investigations may be initiated because:
• the results of a fit and proper assessment indicate fit and proper concerns, and the application is referred for a
fit and proper investigation by licensing staff,
• a licence application requires automatic referral for a fit and proper investigation, or
• branch staff identify fit and proper concerns relating to an existing licensee and the Provincial Director
Compliance and Enforcement approves a fit and proper investigation.

This section outlines the procedures that govern the conduct of fit and proper assessments and investigations,
from receipt of a complete application or information that raises fit and proper concerns, through to investigation
and documentation of any fit and proper allegations in a staff report. The applicable procedures differ somewhat
depending upon whether the fit and proper process is initiated because of an application, or because the branch
receives information that raises fit and proper concerns regarding an existing licensee who has not made any
application to the branch. The two sets of procedures are presented in this section under the following chapter
headings:
• Assessments and Investigations of Applicants, and
• Investigations of Existing Licensees Independently of an Application.

heading: 48.1 Assessments and investigations of applicants
text:
This section outlines the procedures that branch staff will follow when conducting fit and proper assessments and
investigations of applicants. The procedures are organized as 7 general tasks that are consecutively numbered
from 1 to 7. The general tasks are:
1. Conducting a fit and proper assessment and deciding whether to request a fit and proper investigation for a
new liquor primary licence application,
2. Conducting a fit and proper assessment and deciding whether to request a fit and proper investigation for an
application other than a new liquor primary licence application,
3. Assigning a fit and proper investigation to an investigator,
4. Managing licence renewals during a fit and proper investigation,
5. Conducting a fit and proper investigation,
6. Documenting the results of a fit and proper investigation, and
7. Reviewing a staff report of a fit and proper investigation.

new liquor primary licence application
In this task, licensing staff responsible for new liquor primary licence applications conduct a fit and proper
assessment of the application and, if required, refer the application for a fit and proper investigation.

heading: 49.0 Introduction
text:
Once the registrar receives a staff report alleging that an applicant or licensee is not fit and proper, the fit and
proper determination process begins. The process ends once the general manager or delegate determines whether
the applicant or licensee is fit and proper and, in the case of an existing licensee, the appropriate action. It is then
the responsibility of the Licensing Division to implement the decision.
In general, fit and proper determinations will be made after a hearing conducted by an adjudicator, either orally or
via written submissions. In the situation where the applicant or licensee does not dispute the fit and proper
allegations, the general manager or delegate will make a determination without a hearing. The fit and proper
hearing process is similar to the enforcement hearing process, except that fit and proper hearings and decisions are
not open to the public.
49.1 Fit and Proper determinations
This chapter of the manual outlines the procedures that branch staff will follow in making determinations of
whether an applicant or licensee is fit and proper. The procedures are organized as 3 general tasks, numbered
consecutively from 13 to 15. The tasks are:
13. Informing an applicant or licensee of fit and proper allegations
14. Making a determination of whether an applicant or licensee is fit and proper, and
15. Implementing a fit and proper decision.

Date Licence #
